Title: Enhancing group recommendation performance by integrating individual prediction uncertainty
Authors: Fuguo Zhang and Yunhe Liu and Shaoying Feng
Abstract: The uncertainty in the prediction of a single rating by recommender systems can vary significantly owing to the diverse historical interaction data between users and items under a given recommendation model. In group recommendations, high uncertainty in individual rating predictions may lead to erroneous group decisions. However, previous studies have often overlooked the impact of the uncertainty of individual rating predictions in the group recommendation process. To address this, this study proposes a measurement method for individual prediction certainty that employs the validity of bipartite graph voting. In addition, a group recommendation algorithm named consideration member reliability group recommendation (CMRGR), which integrates the individual prediction uncertainty of each group member, is presented. The results of experiments on the MovieLens-1M, Netflix, and MovieTweetings datasets show that the CMRGR algorithm improved the recommendation accuracy by at least 10% compared with the baseline. Moreover, incorporating the prediction uncertainty into recommendations was found to have approximately twice the impact on group recommendation accuracy compared with individual recommendation accuracy.
Keywords: Group recommendation, Individual rating prediction, Uncertainty, Bipartite graph, Voting validity

Title: Equivalence class and modified Gaussian methods for normalization of time series data on AI models
Authors: Savitha K.N. and Linu Pinto and Sasi Gopalan and P. Balasubramaniam
Abstract: In data analysis and signal processing, normalization is an essential preprocessing step. The selection of an optimal normalization strategy is a complex process. The paper addresses a common property of normalization functions and its impact on classification and regression models in Deep Learning. The paper also introduces a non-linear normalization function called L-R Gaussian scalar and establishes its similarities in comparison with the Minmax scalar, Maxabs scalar, Standard scalar, and Robust scalar. Experimental analysis shows that the L-Gaussian scalar provides at least 3.5% higher accuracy and the R-Gaussian scalar provides at least 2.3% higher accuracy in the classification of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals compared to the Minmax, Maxabs, Robust and Standard scalar. The paper theoretically establishes that a non negative scaling parameter and any real valued translation parameter generates equivalent signals for the given Time Series data without altering its equivalence classes and experimentally proved to have better performance on classification and regression models in Deep neural networks. Results show that equivalent signals give at least 12.5% higher accuracy on classification performance with a scaling parameter of 0.5 and translation parameter 0 and at least 1.2% lower MAE values on prediction with noisy data with a scaling parameter of 0.3 and translation parameter 0 compared to the Minmax, Maxabs, Standard and Robust scalar. The study reveals that all normalization functions give an equivalence relation and partition the dataset into the same equivalence classes except for Maxabs scalar, and each class is mapped to its corresponding normalized vector. Theoretical analysis proves that the non-linear normalization functions, L-Gaussian and R-Gaussian scalar, provides the exact equivalence class representation as the linear normalization functions Minmax, Robust and Standard scalar. Experimental results show that L-Gaussian which is the reversed peak representation of the R-Gaussian scalar gives better performance on signals having larger low range values compared to high range values and does not alter the equivalence class representation of the original signal. The Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and Percent Root Mean Square Difference (PRD) metrics evaluate the efficiency of the L-R Gaussian scalar in comparison with other scalars for noise reduction. Also, SNR, RMSE, and PRD bounds on L-R Gaussian function are optimal compared to the other scalars. Experimental analysis of the electrocardiogram (ECG) dataset shows that for the L-Gaussian scalar, denoising performance reaches up to 40% on SNR values and 83% on PRD values. In contrast, the R-Gaussian scalar shows denoising performance up to 10% on SNR values and 37% on PRD values compared to the Minmax scalar.
Keywords: Normalization, Equivalence class, Gaussian function, Time series data, Deep learning, Noise reduction

Title: Traffic congestion predictor: A spatiotemporal graph neural network with congestion-conditional adaptive mechanism and optimization algorithm
Authors: Yutian Liu and Jian Gong and Tianjin Huang and Jinde Cao
Abstract: This paper addresses the underexplored challenge of traffic congestion prediction, a problem frequently encountered in practice yet difficult to model accurately in the literature. Precise congestion prediction is essential for effective traffic management and the implementation of proactive control strategies. To tackle this, we introduce TC-Predictor, a novel neural network architecture that integrates a congestion-conditional adaptive graph convolutional network (GCN). This mechanism captures both the global road network structure and local dynamic patterns, while dynamically adjusting the adjacency matrix based on congestion levels at each prediction step. Additionally, we introduce a data-driven metric that prioritizes infrequent but critical traffic data, thereby emphasizing high-traffic scenarios. Furthermore, the sparrow search algorithm (SSA) is employed for hyperparameter optimization, with an added congestion constraint in its objective function. Empirical evaluations on real-world datasets show that while many deep learning models perform adequately under low congestion, their accuracy significantly deteriorates under high congestion levels. In contrast, TC-Predictor consistently outperforms these models, particularly in predicting congestion under heavy traffic conditions.
Keywords: Traffic congestion, Adaptive mechanism, Graph convolution network, Traffic prediction, Causal inference, Sparrow search algorithm

Title: A comprehensive survey on techniques for numerical similarity measurement
Authors: Surendra Gupta and Urjita Thakar and Sanjiv Tokekar
Abstract: Similarity measures are a fundamental component of various data analysis and machine learning tasks, including clustering, classification, and recommender systems. With the growing scale, diversity and complexity of data, selecting the appropriate similarity measure has become a crucial step in achieving accurate results. Over the course of about three hundred years of development, a number of numerical similarity measurement techniques based on various machine learning and data analysis mechanisms have been proposed. Despite significant advancements in the field, a thorough and unified overview of cutting-edge developments in numerical similarity measures is lacking. The objective of this survey is to provide a comprehensive and structured overview of numerical similarity measurement techniques, thereby bridging the existing gap in the literature. This includes historical methods such as Euclidean, Manhattan, Pearson, Spearman, Jaccard, and Cosine measures, as well as newer techniques like transformers and attention mechanisms. This survey paper present taxonomy of current progresses and classify them into four groups: (1) correlation-based numerical similarity measures, (2) distance-based numerical similarity measures, (3) probability-based numerical similarity measures, and (4) set-based numerical similarity measures. The mathematical foundations, benefits, and limitations of each technique, as well as their applications in a variety of disciplines are discussed. This survey paper also highlights the integration of transformer and attention mechanisms with various similarity measures, including graph-based, hybrid, fuzzy-based, and kernelized approaches, among others. These methodologies enhance the accuracy and robustness of similarity assessments by capturing complex relationships and contextual nuances in data. Furthermore, the challenges and future research directions in developing new numerical similarity measures that can effectively handle high-dimensional complex data, heterogeneous data types, and capturing nonlinear relationships have been highlighted. This survey is intended to provide a comprehensive guide for academics and professionals in selecting and applying appropriate numerical similarity measures in their work.
Keywords: Similarity measures, Distance-based measures, Correlation-based measures, Set-based measures, Probability-based measures, Data analysis, Machine learning, Information retrieval

Title: Economic implications of enhanced stock market analysis using improved forecasting methods
Authors: Jinqian Peng and Yuming Yang
Abstract: Stock price forecasting in financial markets is a very challenging task, mainly because of the inherent nonlinearity and nonstationary of stock price time series, which are influenced by many dynamic factors. This paper proposes a novel hybrid model to overcome these challenges effectively. The model integrates Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD), Sample Entropy (SE), Slime Mould Algorithm (SMA), Extreme Learning Machine (ELM), and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (BiGRU). Using a decade-long dataset of the CSI 300 index, with daily prices and trading volumes the model demonstrated highly accurate performance. The development of the proposed EMD-SE-ELM-SMA-BiGRU process first starts with data decomposition using EMD, which decomposes these complex financial time series into simpler intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). Then, these IMFs are clustered by SE into four different sequences of high, medium, low, and residual. The ELM model is used for the processing of the high-frequency sequence due to its capability of detecting rapid variations, while the rest of the sequences are handled by the SMA-BiGRU model to capture long-term dependencies and relations. The proposed hybrid model, on the CSI 300, achieved an R2 value of 0.9823. Additionally, the model demonstrated its adaptability to other global indices by obtaining R2 values of 0.9853 for Apple stock, 0.9905 for the BSE index, 0.9917 for Crude Oil price, 0.9918 for Gold price, 0.9816 for HSI, and 0.9928 for the Nasdaq index. The results underscore the effectiveness of the EMD-SE-ELM-SMA-BiGRU model in discerning intricate market dynamics, as a way to enhance the precision of stock price forecasts and to offer insights useful for policymakers and investors operating in different market conditions.

Title: Mapping stock market dynamics: A tripartite neural network approach using modified grid search for stock market prediction
Authors: Singh S.; Singh M.; Attri S.
Abstract: The challenge of stock market prediction still persists for investors, researchers, portfolio managers, and a diverse array of stakeholders. This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of artificial neural networks, deep neural networks, and long-term memory models in predicting stock market indices. The study encompasses daily index prices of Nifty 50, S&P 500, and Euronext 100, along with macroeconomic data and technical indicators from January 2015 to September 2023, containing 2201 observations for each market. When evaluated using different metrics, the results indicate better performance of artificial neural network models than deep neural networks and long short-term memory models in most cases. The results from the validation set, test set, and an extra holdout set indicate better performance of artificial neural networks in the context of the Nifty 50 index. In the case of the S&P 500, the deep neural network performed well on validation set results, and artificial neural networks performed better than other models in the test set and holdout set predictions. In the case of Euronext 100, the deep neural network again performed better on the validation set; however, the Long short-term memory model outperformed other models with better predictions on testing and holdout set data. Title: A hybrid optimized deep learning model via the Golden Jackal Optimizer for accurate stock price forecasting
Authors: Gkonis V.; Tsakalos I.
Abstract: Stock markets have historically been the reference point of the worldwide financial environment throughout the years. Investing in the stock market carries risk; however, it can offer significant short- or long-term returns for the investor. Forecasting stock prices has been a vital topic among professionals and researchers; however, it has always been a difficult task. Machine learning and metaheuristic algorithms over the last years have shown remarkable performance in a variety of sectors, encompassing the financial sector. Title: Enhancing futures price forecasting with large-scale text feature extraction and compressed hybrid data-driven modeling
Authors: Lingyao Zhu and Huwei Liu and Junhui Zhao and Kaibo Liang and Li Zhou and Jianglong Yang
Abstract: This paper proposes a large-scale text information extraction and hybrid structured data interpretability analysis approach, with the aim of enhancing futures price prediction in China. Specifically, this study collects and analyzes both structured time series data and unstructured text data related to soybean meal futures from 2015 to 2022. For structured data modeling, time series models such as ARIMAX, LSTM, and TCN are compared, and supervised learning models such as XGBoost and LightGBM demonstrate superior performance. For unstructured data, word embedding models such as RoBERTa and TinyBERT are utilized to extract semantic features from news and research reports. A compressed hybrid model combining structured data with 128-dimensional TinyBERT text features is constructed and further enhanced by adding technical indicator features. The hybrid model with compressed text features achieves improved performance and interpretability. To verify the real-world effectiveness, quantitative trading strategies are constructed based on the model predictions, and historical data backtesting shows positive returns. The proposed approach combining large-scale text feature extraction, compressed hybrid modeling and enhanced structured data achieves significant accuracy improvements in futures price forecasting compared to baseline models, providing a valuable reference for fusing multi-source data to enhance predictive analytics.

Title: A multi-feature selection fused with investor sentiment for stock price prediction
Authors: Zhen K.; Xie D.; Hu X.
Abstract: The stock market data has the characteristics of high dimensionality and multiple noise, and the investment behavior of investors is easily influenced by emotions, which poses a great challenge to stock price prediction. To improve the accuracy of stock price prediction, this study proposes a combined modeling approach based on multiple feature selection algorithms and incorporating investor sentiment. First, we collected stock trading data of the Chinese A-share market from 2018 to 2022, and three types of investor sentiment data sourced from social media, Internet news and newspaper news. Then, we used five feature selection algorithms to select dozens of important features from hundreds of features in the stock trading data. Based on three types of investor sentiment data, five sentiment indicators were constructed and included in the subsequent feature selection along with the previously selected important features. Finally, five deep learning models were used to predict stock prices using feature sets with sentiment indicators. A total of 1030 stocks from 10 industries such as pharmaceutical and biological, leisure service, food and beverage were selected for the experiment. The results show that in 10 industries, LSTM-CNN-Attention model has the best effect on stock price prediction, and after incorporating the sentiment indicator constructed by the principal component, the effect of the model is significantly improved, and the performance is the best in 7 industries. Title: Predicting risk/reward ratio in financial markets for asset management using machine learning
Authors: Yarbakhsh R.; Soleymani Baghshah M.; Karimaghaie H.
Abstract: Financial market forecasting remains a formidable challenge despite the surge in computational capabilities and machine learning advancements. Title: Effect of exogenous market sentiment indicators in stock price direction prediction
Authors: Keun Yun M.K.
Abstract: As the most popular methodology in stock price prediction, technical analysis accounts for 66 % of stock price prediction studies for 11 years’ period (2007 ∼ 2018), meanwhile fundamental analysis and combined analysis using technical and fundamental analysis are just 23 % and 11 % of studies, respectively. Technical stock price analysis generally expands the feature space by generating price-derived technical indicators from daily stock prices. However, using price-derived technical indicators is criticized for its complete subjectivity and self-fulfilling prophecy. As a remedial action for price-derived technical indicators, this study includes three popular exogenous market sentiment indicators (EMIs): market volatility index (VIX), fear-greed index (FGX), and put-call ratio (PCR), and investigates the importance and effect of the selected EMIs in stock price direction prediction. To capture the maximal effect of the EMIs in stock price direction prediction, the best feature subset (BFS) selection method is adopted in company with the extreme gradient boosting (XGB) algorithm, which significantly improves the prediction accuracy and interpretability with fewer input features. The proposed BFS with XGB method adequately reflects the collective behaviour of the EMIs with price-derived technical indicators of time series stock price data. Title: An approach to stock price prediction based on improved EEMD and attention-enhanced BiLSTM
Authors: Zhinzhong Liu and Zhaohui Su and Ling Shang and Hongxiang Sun and Bin Zhao
Abstract: Accurate stock price prediction is a urgently needed technology in economic investment. However, stock prices are influenced by various factors and display non-linear and non-stationary characteristics, which make accurately predicting stock prices a critical challenge. To tackle the above issue, we propose a method for stock price prediction based on improved ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) and attention-enhanced BiLSTM (AEBiLSTM), referred to as SPPEA. First, to reduce the nonlinearity of the stock prices and improve the prediction accuracy, our method first divides the original stock price series into subsequences with the same time scale using a sliding window. These sub-sequences are then decomposed into multiple intrinsic mode Function (IMF) components with the EEMD method which is improved by cubic spline interpolation. Then, the decomposed IMF components are input into AEBiLSTM to capture the dependencies of stock price data and the features of important points of the stock prices, and then the prediction results of each IMF component are obtained with AEBiLSTM. Finally, the prediction results of each component are integrated to obtain the final prediction results. Extensive experiments have been conducted on three stock datasets: BYD, China Unicom and Ping An Bank. Experimental results prove that our proposed method has better performance compared with the state-of-the-art methods.

Title: Investigating the impact of sentiments on stock market using digital proxies: Current trends, challenges, and future directions

Abstract: Social media and online news have emerged as significant sources of market sentiment, influencing stock market dynamics globally. Additionally, publicly available benchmark datasets for social media and news sentiment indices are compiled and analyzed, with insights into their limitations and potential improvements. A comparative evaluation of prediction methods across heterogeneous user-generated datasets is performed, identifying the most effective techniques for various data types and problem formulations. Recommendations are offered for selecting suitable techniques based on the nature of the data and the specific problem formulation. Title: A novel inter-intra graph neural networks for stock price forecasting modeling cross-border relationships
Authors: Bukhari M.; Maqsood M.; Sattar A.
Abstract: The applications of artificial intelligence for streamlining different financial services referred to as financial technology (FinTech), are now being expanded to include modernized approaches. Existing research studies mainly use machine learning (ML) or deep learning (DL) architectures, which are mainly concerned with capturing temporal relationships. Nevertheless, these methodologies ignore the fundamental relationships between stocks resulting in limited performance. However, they are still limited to focusing on single-stock market scenarios and disregarding the cross-market or cross-border correlations that exist among global financial systems. This constraint impairs their ability to represent the interconnectedness of various financial sectors and marketplaces. Hence, this study proposed a MEIG (Macro-Event Driven Inter-Intra Graph) model to exploit both inter-and intra-relationships among the stocks as well as modeling of intra-inter event sentiment dynamics of 42.74 million tweets and the impact of macroeconomics. The proposed model utilizes stock price correlations to assess regional interactions completely. In addition, to manage the interplay between inter and intra graphs, the Cross-Graph Attention Layer (CGAT) is also proposed to weigh the importance of stock connections within their respective intra-inter market networks. For experimentation, stock markets including SP500, SSE-50, KSE-50, BIST-100, and FTSE-100 are utilized as a pair to demonstrate differing levels of correlations such as between developed economies, superpower economies, developed to emerging economies, and emerging to emerging economies. The proposed MEIG model shows improved results in comparison with baseline methods by obtaining the lowest MSE error of 0.0009 respectively. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A metal price forecasting framework optimized with TLBO metaheuristic and selective for highest returns
Authors: Shih-Hsien Tseng and Manh-Hung Nguyen
Abstract: Metal price prediction constitutes a significant economic challenge. Fluctuations in metal prices substantially impact various industries, including manufacturing, construction, energy, and transportation. Accurate price predictions enable organizations to make informed decisions, optimize operations, and mitigate risks, thereby enhancing competitiveness and profitability. The proposed framework is designed to process time series price data with the target output including trend predictions and recommended actions for each day to achieve the highest return. In this study, we investigate various machine learning algorithms, including linear regression, logistic regression, Artificial Neural Networks, Long Short-Term Memory, and XGBoost, for both classification and regression output. This research employs Empirical Mode Decomposition to generate decomposed series, termed Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs), from close price time series data. Subsequently, these IMFs are utilized as feature vectors for prediction models. To optimize returns in trading decisions, the study applies the TLBO algorithm to determine the optimized learning rate, training and validation datasets, and SHRV method to select the models that achieve the highest return at validation. Through validation on empirical datasets from seven distinct metals markets over several years, the EMD-TLBO-SHRV framework demonstrates superior performance compared to traditional models in terms of both predictive accuracy and simulated trading returns. This research offers a practical and scalable approach to commodity price forecasting in volatile market conditions.

Title: Robust kernel-free double well potential twin support vector regression
Authors: Boyu Ma and Xingmei Li and Guowei Zhang
Abstract: Twin support vector regression (TSVR) has demonstrated superior computational efficiency compared with SVR and has been extensively applied across various fields. However, the performance of TSVR could be significantly deteriorated by outliers because of the utilization of the L2 norm loss function. We propose a robust kernel-free quartic surface TSVR model to address this issue by utilizing a novel robust loss function and the double well potential (DWP) function. The proposed robust loss function combines the L1 and L2 norm loss functions through a hyperparameter designed to be robust against outliers. The proposed double well potential TSVR (DWPTSVR) extends the application of the kernel-free DWP function in TSVR for the first time. Unlike conventional kernel methods that require time-consuming kernel parameter searching, the proposed DWPTSVR model eliminates this step by predefining a nonlinear surface. Extensive experimental results indicate that the proposed DWPTSVR outperforms previous well-established kernel-based or kernel-free SVR and TSVR models in terms of accuracy and robustness on ten artificial datasets and eight benchmark datasets with different types of outliers. The sensitivity analysis results reveal that the proposed DWPTSVR model with the combination of L1 and L2 norm loss functions performs significantly better than the model with L1 or L2 norm loss functions. Moreover, the proposed DWPTSVR model is validated to be successfully applied in two time series datasets and three large-scale real-world datasets. In addition, an efficient version of DWPTSVR is also developed to deal with large-scale high-dimensional datasets.

Title: Leveraging data-driven machine learning techniques to enhance bearing capacity estimation in prebored and precast piles
Authors: Seunghwan Seo and Gunwoong Kim and Jong-Bae Park and Juhyong Kim and Yong-Boo Park and Moonkyung Chung
Abstract: The rapid pace of urbanization and the increasing demand for reliable deep foundation systems in metropolitan areas necessitate advanced methodologies for accurately predicting the bearing capacity of pile foundations. This study presents a novel application of machine learning (ML) techniques to estimate the pile bearing capacity (PBC) of prebored and precast piles (PPP) constructed with pretensioned prestressed high-strength concrete (PHC). Unlike traditional approaches that rely on empirical dynamic driving formulas, this research explores the potential of ML models to provide more accurate and practical solutions for construction quality control. Three ML algorithms—K-Nearest Neighbor Regression (KNR), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), and Deep Neural Networks (DNN)—were employed to predict PBC at two critical stages of PPP installation: the End of Initial Driving (EOID) and Restrike phases. A dataset comprising 217 dynamic load tests was used for model development and validation. The results demonstrate that the ML models, particularly the DNN, significantly outperform traditional dynamic driving formulas such as the Hiley, Danish, and Gates methods in terms of both prediction accuracy and generalization capability. The DNN model achieved R2 values of 0.960 for EOID and 0.915 for Restrike phase predictions, with minimal prediction errors across varying site conditions. Importantly, this study introduces a direct comparison between AI-driven models and conventional formulas, providing empirical evidence that ML-based predictions are less susceptible to the overestimations and underestimations often observed in traditional methods. Furthermore, interpretability was enhanced through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), which identified key influencing factors, such as pile diameter and ram weight, offering valuable insights for on-site decision-making and adaptive control during pile driving operations. By validating ML predictions against field-tested PDA results and widely used empirical formulas, this research establishes the practical feasibility of integrating AI into existing construction workflows. The proposed ML approach not only enhances prediction reliability but also streamlines quality control processes, reducing dependence on empirical judgments and contributing to more efficient and cost-effective project delivery.

Title: Unveiling risk propagation: a lead-lag-aware framework for financial market prediction
Authors: Xiao S.; Li Q.; Gong X.; Zhao J.; Gu L.; Peng L.
Abstract: Recent studies have highlighted that the relationships between firms play a pivotal role in improving the accuracy of financial time series prediction. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), which model the structured relationships among firms, have shown great potential in capturing the dynamic characteristics of financial time series. However, existing studies often assume uniform risk propagation paths between firms, failing to capture the diverse and evolving risk contagion patterns inherent in real-world financial systems. To address these challenges, this work proposes CGLR, which aims to decouple lead-lag temporal relationships and dynamically represent the message passing process to capture dynamic, multi-level risk propagation. CGLR first employs an attention mechanism to identify significant relationships and efficiently disentangle lead-lag effects using cross-correlation and Fast Fourier Transform. Subsequently, these decoupled lead-lag relationships are embedded into the message passing process, where the model adaptively selects optimal pathways for aggregating risk contagion based on the inferred temporal dependencies. By capturing multi-level risk propagation patterns, our model ensures an accurate representation of complex inter-stock dynamics. Experiments on real-world datasets from the Chinese A-share market show that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing benchmarks in key metrics, including the coefficient of determination (R2), Rank Information Coefficient (Rank IC), and the Information Ratio of Rank IC (Rank ICIR). These results highlight the effectiveness of our framework and its potential for practical applications in real-time financial forecasting. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

Title: TFE-HMM: Combining state transitions and price trends for stock price forecasting
Authors: Xu Yuan and Yi Guo and Shaokui Gu and Jiaqiang Wang and Ange Qi and Shijin Li and Liang Zhao
Abstract: Stock price prediction, a fundamental task in the field of quantitative investing, has garnered widespread attention and deep research from scholars, investors, and governmental institutions. However, traditional prediction methods that directly model and forecast numerical values are not only prone to the influence of noise and outliers but also often fail to capture the underlying state information within time series data and the transition dynamics between these states. To address this issue, we propose a Temporal Feature-Enhanced Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (TFE-HMM). Based on the traditional Gaussian Hidden Markov Model, the proposed model utilizes trend information from historical stock data to construct a Hidden Markov Chain. The derived hidden states are combined with stock price fluctuations to form new temporal features, and reliable neighbors are identified through the calculation of weighted mixed similarity. Subsequently, the price fluctuations of each identified neighbor are weighted and aggregated to produce the final prediction result. Title: The effect of uncertainty index based on sparse method on volatility prediction of stock market

Title: A hierarchical deep learning framework for pair trading with attention and graph networks

Abstract: Pair trading is a market-neutral strategy aimed at generating profits through arbitrage by simultaneously trading correlated assets. Title: Novel approach for deep learning-based market forecasting and portfolio selection incorporating market efficiency

Abstract: Efficient portfolio construction remains a fundamental challenge for investors, especially in market environments that are constantly changing and uncertain. Title: MCNR: Multiscale feature-based latent data component extraction linear regression model

Abstract: Time series forecasting is of great significance in various fields and is widely applied in industries such as finance and energy management. To address this, we propose a multi-scale latent feature extraction model, MCNR, for specific periods. It assigns weighted labels to periodic data points through a backward-weighted periodic module, thereby giving more weight to the periodic points and allowing the model to focus on key periodic features. Another core innovation of the MCNR model is the division of the retrospective window into different scales to capture long-term, mid-term, and short-term time features. For data of different scales, the model uses the Regularized Latent Component Regression (RLC) module for latent component extraction and regularization. Title: Forecasting tourism stock index dynamics: a multiscale deep learning framework integrating emerging media data
Authors: Feng Shen and Shuai Huang and Wanqing Zhao and Dao Lan
Abstract: This study introduces a novel multiscale and multivariable deep learning framework for tourism stock index forecasting. To address the research gap concerning emerging media’s impact on the tourism sector, our study innovatively integrate multi-source data, including Douyin (China’s prominent short video platform), into our predictive model. Our methodology employs a multiscale decomposition strategy to streamline feature extraction complexity, coupled with an enhanced temporal convolutional network model incorporating soft-thresholding denoising to mitigate noise interference. Furthermore, we implement an adaptive differentiated prediction strategy to optimize model flexibility. Empirical analysis utilizing the CSI Tourism Stock Index demonstrates that our proposed model outperforms benchmark models in both predictive accuracy and stability, thereby validating its efficacy in tourism stock index forecasting.
Keywords: Tourism stock index, Time series forecasting, Emerging media data, Multiscale decomposition, Deep learning

Title: Multi-objective portfolio optimization for stock return prediction using machine learning
Authors: Meiyu Huang and Shili Dang and Miraj Ahmed Bhuiyan
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach that integrates stock return prediction with the mean–variance (MV) model to enhance the performance of the original model. Firstly, stock returns are predicted using machine learning algorithms, including Robust Linear Regression (OLS-H), Random Forest (RF), and Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTM), to select a pre-screened stock pool composed of stocks with high predicted returns. Secondly, a linear weighting method combines the predictions above with the MV model, constructing the Mean-Variance-Forecast Error (MVF) model and determining the investment proportions for the pre-selected stocks. Finally, empirical research is conducted using the components of the CSI 300 Index as sample data. The results indicate that the RF + MVF model outperforms other models and the CSI 300 Index in return and risk metrics. At the same time, a sensitivity analysis of relevant parameters further confirms that considering return uncertainty is beneficial for improving the out-of-sample performance of the MV model.
Keywords: Machine learning, Cross-sectional return prediction, Mean-variance, Random forest, Long short-term memory networks

Title: Complex forecasting and investment strategy optimization via chain-of-thought of large language models
Authors: Meiqun Yin and Mengzhu Guo
Abstract: This paper pioneers the application of chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting in large language models (LLMs) for financial forecasting and portfolio optimization. Leveraging anonymized financial statements from 608 Chinese A-share listed companies (2010–2023), we benchmark ChatGPT 4.0 against human analysts in earnings direction prediction. The CoT-enhanced model achieved superior accuracy (64.35% vs. 58.37%) and generated a 17.14% alpha with a Sharpe ratio of 1.5959 in backtests, demonstrating LLMs’ capacity to automate financial reasoning while reducing reliance on specialized expertise. Our findings bridge AI and quantitative finance by validating LLMs’ cross-domain adaptability using purely numerical data, offering practical implications for AI-driven investment decision systems.
Keywords: Large language models, Chain-of-thought, Financial forecasting, Portfolio optimization, Quantitative finance

Title: Stock price trend forecasting based on multi-channel complementary network with CEEMDAN decomposition and transformer residual prediction
Authors: Shen Y.; Dai J.; Wang M.; Arce G.R.
Abstract: Forecasting stock market movement provides important investment signals, but the presence of a large amount of noise in financial time series (FTS) data poses significant challenges to prediction accuracy. This paper proposes a novel multi-channel complementary network with data decomposition and a fusion strategy to effectively improve the prediction accuracy and robustness of stock price movement. The model first applies the algorithm of Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN) to decompose the historical stock data sequence into a set of Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs), representing different frequency components of the original FTS data. Then, each IMF combined with six key indicators (i.e., open price, high price, low price, trading volume, price-earnings ratio and price-to-book ratio) are processed by an independent long short-term memory (LSTM) module to make a parallel prediction. To further enhance the forecasting accuracy, a transformer-based residual term prediction model is incorporated, serving as the complementary branch to the LSTM modules. Subsequently, the outputs from all network branches are fused together to obtain the final prediction result. A set of numerical experiments on different stock index datasets are conducted to verify the superiority of the proposed model in terms of average forecasting accuracy compared with other benchmark models. In addition, the effectiveness of different sub-modules in the proposed framework is proved by the ablation experiments. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd. Title: FinLSPM: Large stock predict model via numerical prior knowledge from LLM
Authors: HongHong Guo and Pak Yin Kwok and Yi Guo and JunWen Zhao and DeFeng Gu
Abstract: In the domain of quantitative investment and market risk management, accurate time series forecasting plays a critical role in ensuring market stability and mitigating systemic risks. However, due to the inherently nonlinear nature of financial data, this field has long faced complex modeling challenges. Recently, large model technologies have demonstrated significant improvements in domains such as meteorology and energy, offering novel solutions to financial forecasting challenges.This study proposes FinLSPM, a cost-effective framework that transforms general-purpose large language model (LLM) into specialized time series forecasting models tailored for financial applications. By leveraging minimal architectural adjustments and efficient parameter tuning, FinLSPM enables the adaptation of LLM with minimal overhead, optimizing them for financial time series forecasting. It achieves enhanced predictive efficiency through two key components: (1) a Numerical Greedy Tokenization (NGT) mechanism that maps inputs into numeric symbol subsets, leveraging the numerical relationship patterns implicitly learned by LLM during large-scale text-based pre-training; and (2) a customized MR-MAE loss function that improves volatility pattern learning during full-parameter fine-tuning. Experimental results demonstrate that in daily-frequency NASDAQ index forecasting tasks, FinLSPM achieves prediction accuracy comparable to or exceeding that of multiple mainstream models, with MAE reduced by 69.8 % compared to the Linear model. Evaluations across multiple financial datasets, including S&P 500 and Bitcoin, confirm its strong generalization. Ablation studies validate the efficacy of each component.
Keywords: Financial time series forecasting, Large language model, NGT Mapping, MR-MAE Loss function

Title: Integrative stock price trend prediction via hierarchical LLM text processing and patch-based transformer with co-attention
Authors: Zhang Y.; Dong Z.; Xu W.
Abstract: Recent advances in large language models have improved semantic extraction; however, existing approaches still struggle to distill truly market-moving signals from lengthy, redundant financial texts, and simple concatenation or one-way cross-attention often fails to capture the bidirectional dependencies between textual semantics and price dynamics. We propose a multimodal framework with hierarchical summarization and co-attention that jointly learns from financial news and historical prices for stock trend prediction. The framework comprises three components. A hierarchical LLM progressively refines text, removing redundancy and extracting multi-level cues most relevant to market movements. A patch-based, single-channel Transformer models price sequences and text streams in parallel, reducing attention complexity while preserving each modality’s temporal and contextual structure. A co-attention mechanism dynamically aligns and reinforces cross-modal features to yield robust joint representations. In experiments, our method achieves 67.01 % directional accuracy with a Matthews Correlation Coefficient of 0.346 on CMIN-US and 70.24 % accuracy with a Matthews Correlation Coefficient of 0.293 on CMIN-CN. Ablation results confirm that combining hierarchical summarization with co-attention substantially improves multimodal forecasting performance. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd. Title: GHOST: Sentiment-gated mamba and stock-wise tokenization attention for enhanced stock prediction
Authors: Zhu W.; Xie L.; Fu H.; Zhang J.
Abstract: Stock trend prediction faces significant challenges due to market sentiment influences, long-term dependencies, and time-varying stock correlation. Specifically, (1) Current sentiment analysis methods exhibit insufficient market sentiment quantification and lack dynamic adaptive integration mechanisms for market fluctuations. (2) Transformer-based models’ quadratic complexity limits long-term stock prediction while lacking finance-specific temporal inductive biases. (3)Traditional temporal tokenization paradigms forcibly merge multi-stock features, weakening stock correlation modeling while dramatically increasing computational costs. To address these constraints, we present GHOST (Gated Hybrid Organization with Sentiment-guided Temporal Mamba and Stock-wise Tokenization Attention). In particular, we leverage GDELT(Global Database of Events, Language and Tone) sentiment quantification through a Hierarchical Sentiment-Gated Layer for dynamic fusion of affective features with trading data. Additionally, Intra-Stock Mamba Selection Layer achieves time-series linear complexity for long-term forecasting by combining a dynamically parameterized shared state space model to provide specialized financial inductive biases. Moreover, our Stock-wise Tokenization Layer converts temporal tokens into stock tokens while preserving data integrity, enabling Inter-Stock Attention Layer to capture stock correlation via attention between stock tokens and reducing attention computation complexity. Experimental results on real-world stock datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our model. Title: Transforming machine learning strategies in quantitative stock investment: A multisource information fusion and online ensemble modeling approach for superior alpha factors
Authors: Zhao Y.; Chen Z.; Cao C.; Li Y.; Ying J.; Mu J.; Yang C.
Abstract: The real-world stock market environment offers opportunities for short-term prediction and arbitrage using machine learning techniques, with alpha factors playing a crucial role in this process. However, alpha factor models based on machine learning are currently facing key challenges, such as the limited modeling data sources and the inadequate adaptability to dynamic market conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a two-stage multisource information fusion and online ensemble modeling (MSIF-OEM) framework. This framework employs a parallel network architecture to extract temporal features from multisource trading data, including basic stock open, high, low, close, and volume (OHLCV) data, market snapshot data, limit order book (LOB) data and trade and quote (TAQ) data, and leverages ensemble learning and online learning techniques to synthesize alpha factors in real-time based on the extracted temporal features. Experiments conducted on full data from China’s A-share stock market demonstrate that the alpha factors synthesized by the MSIF-OEM framework exhibit significantly superior predictive performance. Furthermore, a detailed investigation of the framework’s components reveals several key insights that offer valuable guidance to the future development of machine learning strategies in quantitative stock investment. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Hybrid multivariate time series prediction system based on PD-XGBoost-KRVFL
Authors: Lijun Sun and Feng Qin
Abstract: Multivariate time series prediction (MTSP) plays a vital role in information fusion and is widely applied in complex systems such as finance, environmental monitoring, and intelligent control. Although the kernel random vector functional-link (KRVFL) network has shown competitive performance in MTSP tasks, it still faces two primary challenges when dealing with high-dimensional time series data. First, existing models lack robust mechanisms for quantifying uncertainty in expansive feature spaces and efficient frameworks for feature selection. Second, the training process does not fully exploit the importance of samples, thereby limiting further improvements in predictive accuracy. To address these limitations, we propose a hybrid modeling framework-PD-XGBoost-KRVFL-that integrates possibility theory with ensemble learning strategies to enhance the modeling capabilities for multivariate time series. Specifically, the framework initially applies localized Gaussian membership functions to transform raw data into a possibility distribution (PD). It then constructs a multidimensional feature selection scheme by combining fuzzy entropy, fuzzy mutual information, and the Jensen-Shannon divergence for robust feature evaluation and redundancy suppression. In addition, a dynamic sample weighting mechanism based on extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) residual correction is designed to recalibrate sample importance and guide the KRVFL training process more effectively. By jointly optimizing feature selection and model learning, the PD-XGBoost-KRVFL framework achieves enhanced predictive performance. Across five real-world financial datasets, the proposed model ranks first in TIC and Willmott Index on all datasets, and achieves the lowest RMSE, MAE, MAPE, SMAPE, and highest R2 on four datasets (second on Mortgage). Relative to the best-performing baseline on each dataset, it reduces these error metrics by 11.9% (RMSE on Treasury vs. BPNN) to 82.5% (MAPE on Stock vs. BPNN), with the largest gains observed under high volatility and nonlinearity, demonstrating robust accuracy, stability, and generalization in multi-source financial time-series forecasting.
Keywords: Multivariate time series prediction, Possibility theory, Extreme gradient boosting, Kernel random vector functional-link network

Title: Quantformer: From attention to profit with a quantitative transformer trading strategy
Authors: Zhang Z.; Chen B.; Zhu S.; Langrené N.
Abstract: In traditional quantitative trading practice, navigating the complicated and dynamic financial market presents a persistent challenge. Fully capturing various market variables, including long-term information, as well as essential signals that may lead to profit remains a difficult task for learning algorithms. In order to tackle this challenge, this paper introduces quantformer, an enhanced neural network architecture based on transformer, to build investment factors. By borrowing ideas from sentiment analysis, quantformer not only exploits its original inherent advantages in capturing long-range dependencies and modeling complex data relationships, but is also able to solve tasks with numerical inputs and accurately forecast future returns over a given period. This work collects more than 5,000,000 rolling data of 4601 stocks in the Chinese capital market from 2010 to 2023. The results of this study demonstrate the model’s superior performance in predicting stock trends compared with other 100-factor-based quantitative strategies. Notably, the model’s innovative use of transformer-like model to establish factors, in conjunction with market sentiment information, has been shown to enhance the accuracy of trading signals significantly, thereby offering promising implications for the future of quantitative trading strategies. Title: Enhancing stock price forecasting with a modular deep learning framework incorporating plug-and-play transformer variants
Authors: Huang Y.; Yang C.
Abstract: Stock price forecasting remains challenging due to highly nonstationary, noisy financial time-series punctuated by rare extreme events with persistent impacts. Although recent deep-learning models, especially CNNs, RNNs, and Transformers, have improved predictive accuracy, they still face significant limitations regarding distributional drift, tail-risk robustness, and computational demands for long sequences. To bridge these gaps, we propose a modular, knowledge-driven deep learning framework integrating Reversible Instance Normalization (RevIN), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), plug-and-play Transformer variants, and Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM). RevIN acts as an expert-driven decision-support module, dynamically normalizing data to mitigate regime shifts while maintaining outputs in economically meaningful scales. CNN captures local temporal micro-patterns, Transformer variants (standard Transformer, iTransformer, etc.) handle global temporal and cross-variable dependencies, and BiLSTM fuses forward-backward temporal dynamics. The fully modular, plug-and-play architecture enables effortless incorporation of emerging Transformer variants without retraining existing components, ensuring long-term adaptability and scalability. Empirical evaluations on four cross-market datasets (NASDAQ-AAPL, NASDAQ-MSFT, SSE-600519, and HKEX-00005) confirm that our framework significantly lowers RMSE and MAPE by up to 50% and 54%, respectively, compared with five strong baselines. These performance gains are achieved with only a moderate (about 22%) increase in GPU training time and comparable inference latency to lightweight models. Cross-market tests further demonstrate robust generalization across distinct market regimes and currencies, significantly outperforming baseline models even without retraining. Ablation studies validate the complementary contribution of each module, underscoring the effectiveness of integrating expert-driven normalization and modular deep-learning components for robust financial decision-support systems. Title: A neural network informer in algorithmic investment strategies on high-frequency bitcoin data
Authors: Filip Stefaniuk and Robert Ślepaczuk
Abstract: The article investigates the usage of the Informer architecture for building automated trading strategies for high-frequency Bitcoin data. Three strategies using the Informer model with different loss functions: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Generalized Mean Absolute Directional Loss (GMADL), and Quantile loss, are proposed and evaluated against the Buy and Hold benchmark and two benchmark strategies based on technical indicators. The evaluation is conducted using data of various frequencies: 5-min, 15-min, and 30-min intervals, over the 6 different periods. Although the Informer-based model with Quantile loss did not outperform the benchmark, two other models achieved better results. The performance of the model using RMSE loss worsens when used with higher frequency data, while the model that uses the novel GMADL loss function benefits from higher frequency data. When trained on 5-min intervals, it beats all the other strategies on most of the testing periods. The primary contribution of this study is the application and assessment of the RMSE, GMADL, and Quantile loss functions with the Informer model to forecast future returns, subsequently using these forecasts to develop automated trading strategies. The research provides evidence that employing an Informer model trained with the GMADL loss function can result in superior trading outcomes compared to the Buy&Hold approach.
Keywords: Machine learning, Financial series forecasting, Automated trading strategy, Informer, Transformer, Bitcoin, High-frequency trading, Statistics, GMADL

Title: Learning to understand financial risk contagion from a frequency-domain graph learning framework
Authors: Sanchuan Xiao and Jingmei Zhao and Rui Cheng and Yang Wang and Shaofei Shen and Qing Li
Abstract: Understanding and predicting financial risk contagion is paramount for effective risk management and investment decision-making. Although the effectiveness of deep graph learning in this area is widely recognised, existing methods are confined to time-domain frameworks and struggle to capture contagion pathways beyond the most direct or synchronous ones. This makes it difficult to resolve the risk propagation anomalies that are inherent in financial markets. To overcome this limitation, we propose a Finance Frequency-Domain Graph Neural Network, an end-to-end graph learning framework based on the frequency domain. Specifically, (1) a knowledge-guided paradigm alignment module performs spectral calibration via learnable market frequency prototypes to project stock features into a unified semantic space; (2) a dynamic relation inference mechanism distills risk contagion pathways by quantifying spectral coherence and phase differentials between dominant frequency bands; and (3) a state-aware risk propagation module achieves adaptive modeling of risk evolution by re-routing the flow of risk information based on each node’s unique state. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets from the Chinese and US stock markets demonstrate that our model achieves the best performance in terms of both prediction accuracy and investment metrics, highlighting the effectiveness of frequency-domain modeling.
Keywords: Graph neural networks, Stock market prediction, Risk contagion

Title: Dynamic graph learning for integrating temporal relationships in stock prediction
Authors: Zhang L.; Dai Z.; Zeng Q.; Lin N.; Xia H.; Zhao K.; Zhang M.; Liu S.; Ye G.; Wu J.; Chai H.
Abstract: Stock prediction is challenging due to the uncertainty and volatility of financial markets. Recent studies increasingly adopt deep learning methods to model complex market dynamics. A key characteristic of stock markets is the interdependence of price movements among related companies, which can be naturally modeled using graph neural networks. A significant shortcoming of existing methodologies is that they fail to adequately consider the internal dynamic relationships between stocks. These relationships can be quantified in two distinct ways: distance measured by Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) and lead-lag relationship. DTW represents a technical means of mining the similarity of time series data. The lead-lag relationship is a prominent phenomenon in financial markets. To address these limitations, we propose Dynamic Graph Learning for Integrating Temporal Relationships (DyG4TR), which constructs dynamic relationships and introduces a new horizontal/vertical graph learning architecture to integrate short-term and long-term temporal dependencies. Furthermore, we leverage the momentum effect in financial markets to capture momentum features in stock prediction and calculate the loss of each time slice independently, thereby facilitating more accurate representation learning. By mining the intrinsic and temporal relationships inherent in time series data, our method achieves SOTA performance without the need for additional relationship data. Experiments conducted on the CSI 500 and NASDAQ 100 indices demonstrate that our approach effectively addresses the challenges associated with stock prediction in dynamic and noisy market environments, achieving a maximum improvement of 20.98% in return rate. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A multi-graph learning framework to fuse heterogeneous market information for stock forecasting
Authors: Li Z.; Xiong J.; Wang J.; Tan J.; Du Jardin P.; Deveci M.; Zhong K.
Abstract: Traditional financial studies focused on the fundamental indicators data and financial news to track stock movements. Recent studies have revealed that firm relationships, measuring spillovers from related firms, are also important for stock forecasting. However, previous studies via machine learning mostly relied on incomplete market information and failed to capture the interactions and heterogeneity within multimodal data. In this study, a multi-graph neural network framework (MGNN) is proposed to fuse heterogeneous market information with different data structures, i.e., numerical, textual and graphical representations. With such a design, the unique and heterogeneous nature of multimodal data is well addressed. Specially, a fine-grained event extraction methodology is employed to identify valuable events within a substantial corpus of financial news, thereby ensuring the reliability and quality of the extracted events. Then, an explicit and an implicit graph are constructed to integrate firm relationships with fundamental and news information, respectively. Finally, the distinct spillover effects of fundamental and news information are further integrated using a multi-scale cross-attention dual-branch transformer to capture the joint impact on stock movements. Experiments performed on real market data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach over state-of-the-art algorithms. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: An enhanced risk-aware multi-task learning framework with dual-source sentiment and multi-scale decomposition for robust stock ranking forecasting
Authors: Feng Shen and Jia Kuang and You Hu and Shiting Chen
Abstract: Asset price series in financial markets frequently display pronounced nonlinear and non-stationary characteristics, particularly during market regime shifts. These properties heighten uncertainty in market prediction and complicate portfolio optimization. Existing forecasting models often underutilize sentiment information, inadequately address non-stationarity in time series, and exhibit limited sensitivity to risk factors. To address these challenges, this study introduces Sentiment-VMD-MTL, an enhanced framework that integrates dual-source sentiment indicators and variational mode decomposition (VMD) for feature construction. The framework employs a multi-task learning network with a two-stage multi-head attention mechanism for feature extraction and forecasting. Sentiment indicators derived from news articles and stock forum posts capture a broad spectrum of market sentiment. Combined with financial features, VMD decomposes these inputs into multiple stationary modes, thereby improving the representation of both long-term trends and short-term fluctuations. The two-stage attention mechanism adaptively reweights these modes and highlights critical time steps, reducing noise and amplifying informative signals. Furthermore, a risk-aware auxiliary task is incorporated to enhance predictive stability and portfolio resilience. Empirical analysis of constituent stocks from the CSI 300 and Nasdaq 100 indices demonstrates that Sentiment-VMD-MTL surpasses baseline models and state-of-the-art methods across ranking and backtesting metrics. During adverse market conditions and in large-scale capital allocations, the framework helps enhance return stability and improve risk management. A detailed evaluation of individual components illustrates the specific contributions of dual-source sentiment, multi-scale decomposition, and multi-task learning. This research provides a reference for developing resilient financial forecasting models.
Keywords: Investor sentiment, Portfolio optimization, Multi-scale decomposition, Multitask learning

Title: Enhancing financial market prediction through multi-stage signal decomposition and hybrid machine learning
Authors: John Kamwele Mutinda and Li Yong
Abstract: Forecasting stock indices remains challenging due to nonlinearity, nonstationarity, and multiscale dynamics in financial time series. This study proposes the CEEMDAN-SE-VMD-BiGRU-Ridge framework, a novel hybrid model that integrates hierarchical decomposition and adaptive prediction to improve accuracy. The method applies complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) for initial decomposition into intrinsic mode functions. Sample entropy and K-means clustering classify modes into high-frequency, medium-frequency, low-frequency, and residual groups. Variational mode decomposition (VMD) is then applied specifically to further decompose the high-frequency group, suppressing noise and achieving precise noise separation. Bidirectional gated recurrent units (BiGRU) model the high-frequency decomposed IMFs from VMD and the medium-frequency components, while ridge regression captures stable trends in the low-frequency and residual components. Final forecasts are obtained by adding all component predictions linearly. Out-of-sample evaluation on six major global indices—Financial Times Stock Exchange 100 (FTSE), Shanghai Stock Exchange Composite (SSEC), Standard & Poor’s 500 (S&P 500), Deutscher Aktienindex (DAX), New York Stock Exchange Composite (NYSE), and Hang Seng Index (HSI)—using 70-30 hold-out shows excellent performance. The framework achieves R2 values of 0.9958 (FTSE), 0.9944 (SSEC), 0.9994 (S&P 500), 0.9992 (DAX), 0.9986 (NYSE), and 0.9975 (HSI), with substantially lower root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE), and higher R2 than thirteen benchmark models. Modified Diebold-Mariano tests (M-DM) and Model Confidence Set (MCS) analysis confirm statistical superiority. Backtesting yields higher Sharpe ratios, with robustness validated across splits, three business cycles (pre-pandemic expansion, COVID-19 recession, post-crisis recovery), and two contrasting market regimes (COVID-19 stimulus bullish phase, Russia-Ukraine conflict bearish period) as well as varying temporal lookback window. These results highlight the effectiveness of hierarchical decomposition and adaptive deep learning for precise financial forecasting and investment applications.
Keywords: Financial forecasting, Hybrid model, Complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise, Variational mode decomposition, Bidirectional gated recurrent units, Ridge regression

Title: MCMamba: A multi-scale correlation-aware model with Mamba for stock price forecasting
Authors: Fan S.; Yang B.; Xia W.; Shen F.
Abstract: As an important field of financial analysis, stock price forecasting has attracted considerable attention due to its potential to assist investment decision-making and reduce financial risks. In recent years, Transformer-based models have made progress in this field by modeling temporal dependencies of individual stocks and interactions among different stocks through attention mechanisms. However, existing Transformer-based stock forecasting models still suffer from two issues. Firstly, most methods rely on a fixed temporal window to model stock price sequences, which restricts their ability to capture multi-scale temporal dynamics involving both short-term fluctuations and mid-to-long-term trends. Secondly, although attention mechanisms are effective in modeling dynamic inter-stock interactions, they mainly focus on sample-dependent and transient correlations, making it difficult to preserve relatively stable and global inter-stock relationship structures that exist in financial markets. To address these issues, we propose a stock price forecasting model, A Multi-scale Correlation-aware Model with Mamba for Stock Price Forecasting (MCMamba). MCMamba incorporates two complementary designs. On the one hand, a multi-scale temporal modeling strategy based on the Mamba architecture is introduced to characterize the dynamic behaviors of individual stocks across different temporal scales. By constructing multiple temporal representations from the same input sequence, the model is able to capture both short-term fluctuations and mid-to-long-term trends, thereby alleviating the limitations imposed by fixed temporal windows. On the other hand, a data-driven global correlation matrix is constructed from stock representations to capture coarse-grained and relatively stable inter-stock relationships. This matrix is further integrated as auxiliary relational information into attention-based inter-stock modeling, enabling the model to combine dynamic interactions with some stable global relational information. Experiments conducted on the CSI300 and CSI800 datasets demonstrate that MCMamba outperforms several strong baseline models in forecasting performance on real-world stock datasets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: GBT-BiLSTM: A novel fusion network with granular-ball computing for financial time series forecasting
Authors: Changjun Li and Yonghong Li and Shuang Hu and Sidong Xian and Linyan Zhou
Abstract: Financial time series forecasting remains challenging due to high-frequency fluctuations, strong nonlinearity, and complex temporal dependence. Although deep learning models have been widely adopted in AI4Finance, many existing approaches rely on point-wise sequence modeling and are sensitive to noisy short-term price movements. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Granular-Ball Transformer-BiLSTM (GBT-BiLSTM) model for financial time series forecasting. The proposed method constructs granular-balls from historical target series in the training set, aggregating locally coherent observations into coarse-grained structural representations. A BiLSTM branch captures fine-grained short-term price dynamics, while a Transformer-based granular-ball branch models global relations among ordered granular-balls. An adaptive gated fusion mechanism is further designed to integrate local temporal features and global structural information. Experiments on nine real financial datasets show that GBT-BiLSTM achieves the best performance across MAE, RMSE, MAPE, and R2, compared with representative deep-learning forecasting models. Statistical tests and volatility-regime analysis further confirm its overall competitiveness and robustness under different market conditions. The results demonstrate that granular-ball structural modeling can improve the robustness of financial time series forecasting by reducing local noise while preserving useful temporal patterns.
