At the same time, the prediction performance of data based on weighted PCA dimension reduction in multiple machine learning models has also been significantly improved. In the above data conclusions, the dimensionality reduction method proposed in this paper can effectively improve the accuracy and efficiency of financial data analysis, and has high practical application value.
Keywords: Financial data analysis, principal component analysis, weighted PCA, information preservation, time series characteristics

Title: Research on High Frequency Financial Transaction Data Modeling and Cloud Computing Implementation Based on SSA-GA-BP Model
Authors: Chenyang An
Abstract: This article aims to study the modeling of high-frequency financial trading data and its cloud computing implementationWith the swift advancement of big data, cloud computing, and AI technologies, algorithmic trading has emerged as a crucial tool in today’s financial sector. Especially in high-frequency trading, programmatic trading can capture micro changes in the market in real time, thereby improving the efficiency of trading decisions. To enhance the precision of stock price forecasting in high-frequency trading, this paper presents a forecasting approach utilizing the SSA-GA-BP model.In particular, the BP neural network is initially employed for forecasting stock prices, while the evolutionary method and sparrow optimization algorithm are applied to optimize the weights and thresholds of the network, thereby solving the problems of local extremum and convergence speed of the BP model. Secondly, combining with entanglement morphology, two high-frequency trading strategies were designed and implemented, and the strategies were optimized with the support of SSA-GA-BP model, improving the accuracy of buying and selling point recognition and trading stability. The results from the experiments demonstrate that the suggested model has strong fitting ability in predicting stock prices in high-frequency trading, and the optimized trading strategy can provide a higher Sharpe ratio, demonstrating stable return ability.
Keywords: Neural Network, Genetic Algorithm, Sparrow Search Algorithm, Stock Trading

Title: Financial data prediction based on LSTM model
Authors: Chengkun Liu
Abstract: In order to improve the effectiveness and accuracy of financial data forecasting, this paper first reviewed the traditional methods of financial data forecasting and the prediction models based on machine learning in recent years through literature review, and pointed out the potential advantages of LSTM model in solving the problem of financial time series forecasting. Then the steps of data collection and preprocessing are elaborated, the LSTM prediction model is constructed, and the model architecture, parameter setting and training process are explained in detail. In order to verify the validity and accuracy of the model, an experiment was designed to analyze the performance difference between the LSTM model and other prediction models through comparative experiments. The experimental results show that the LSTM model has high accuracy and stability in financial data prediction, especially in the processing of complex time series data. The research results of this paper not only provide a new and effective method for financial data forecasting, but also provide a useful reference for subsequent relevant research.
Keywords: Financial data forecasting, LSTM model, Prediction model.

Title: Augmenting Bank And Economic Data with Generative Adversarial Networks
Authors: Akash Sedai and Francesca Medda and Thomas Schroeder
Abstract: This study addresses the challenges in projecting capital ratios during high-stress periods due to the scarcity of stress scenario data and the tail behaviour of these ratios. We employ Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for data augmentation to improve the accuracy of capital adequacy ratio projections. By augmenting datasets with synthetic data, we improve model performance across various methodologies. The approach is demonstrated using Bayesian model averaging on data from US banks, showing significant improvements in projection accuracy. This methodology offers valuable insights for both regulators and banks in evaluating capital adequacy during financial crises.
Keywords: banking, regulation, machine learning, GAN

Title: ChronosRL: embeddings-based reinforcement learning agent for financial trading
Authors: Adriano Marabuco de A. Lima and Adriano Lorena Oliveira and Cleber Zanchettin
Abstract: ChronosRL is a reinforcement learning (RL) framework for cryptocurrency trading that integrates transformer-generated embed-dings from the Chronos model. By leveraging pre-trained embeddings that capture complex temporal dependencies and nonlinear patterns, ChronosRL addresses the limitations of handcrafted feature-based strategies. Experiments across six cryptocurrency pairs over fve months show that ChronosRL achieves a mean proft of 102% with a 79% standard deviation, outperforming baselines such as Buy and Hold and Moving Average Bollinger Bands. Operating in a zero-shot setting without fine-tuning, ChronosRL demonstrates strong generalization capabilities. These findings highlight the potential of transformer-based embeddings to enhance RL performance in volatile financial environments, bridging advances in sequential representation learning and algorithmic trading.
Keywords: Foundational Models, Time Series, Reinforcement Learning, Embeddings, Trading

Title: Enhancing Multi-Factor Stock Selection with Transformer Networks: A Comparative Analysis Against Traditional Machine Learning Models
Authors: Siqi Lu and Buyao Song and Guowen Li
Abstract: Traditional multi-factor stock selection models often fail to capture complex non-linear dynamics and long-range dependencies in financial markets. This study addresses these limitations by proposing a Transformer-based model, enhanced with Time2Vec, to predict daily stock returns in the Chinese A-share market (2020-2024). We rigorously compare its performance against traditional machine learning (e.g., OLS, XGBoost) and sequential architectures (LSTM, RNN) within a realistic backtesting framework that includes transaction costs. The Transformer model demonstrated superior performance, achieving a 16.41% annualized excess return, a 0.87 Sharpe ratio, and a 15.02% maximum drawdown, significantly outperforming all benchmarks. These findings validate that the Transformer’s self-attention mechanism is highly effective for modeling complex, long-term interactions among financial factors, offering a more robust methodology for quantitative investment.
Keywords: Multi-factor Models, Transformer, Quantitative Investment, Barra Factors

Title: Deep learning-based stock market prediction using historical price and topic-distributed news sentiment
Authors: Rafi Hazel Tafara and Andrew and Yosepril Zhounggi and Muhammad Fikri Hasani and Ayu Maulina
Abstract: Predicting stock prices remains a challenging task because of the volatile and non-linear nature of financial markets. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning method that combines sentiment and topic modeling of financial news with historical stock data to predict Apple Inc. stock prices. FinBERT is used to obtain sentiment scores and BERTopic is used to derive topic distributions and capture topic-aware sentiment context. These features are aligned on a daily basis and processed in a dual-branch neural architecture. One branch uses either LSTM, GRU, or Temporal CNN (TCNN) to handle historical price sequences, while the other is used to process topic-sentiment vectors. The results show that GRU performs slightly better than the other two models, with the highest R2 (0.9866), the lowest RMSE (2.81), and the lowest MAE (2.27). This study focuses only on Apple stock so it gives a more focused view on how financial news sentiment can affect the price prediction of a single stock. Limitations related to dataset size, computational resources, and real-time data availability are also discussed for future research.
Keywords: Stock Price, LSTM, GRU, TCNN, Sentiment Analysis, BERTopic, FinBERT, Apple Stock, Deep Learning, Financial New

Title: Hybrid Ensemble Model Approaches for Stock Price Forecasting Using LSTM, Random Forest, ARIMA, and Linear Regression as Meta-Learner
Authors: Wisnutomo Adji Nugroho and Fernando Darren Rachman and Brainardo Kenneth Siahu and Irene Anindaputri Iswanto and Setiawan Joddy
Abstract: Predicting stock market price remains a complex and challenging task due to the influence of various financial, economic, and behavioral factors. To address these challenges, numerous machine learning and deep learning techniques such as ARIMA, Random Forest, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) have been proposed. However, each model exhibits inherent strengths and limitations in capturing specific data characteristics. This study proposes a hybrid ensemble framework that integrates ARIMA for linear pattern, Random Forest, for non-linear dependencies, and LSTM for temporal dynamics. A meta-learning strategy based on Linear Regression is implemented to perform weighted ensembling of individual model outputs. The experiment results across five major stocks demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms standalone models. The hybrid ensemble model achieved low MAPE scores of 0.5590 for AAPL, 0.7126 for XOM, and 5.944 for TSLA. Additionally, the MAE results across three stocks were 0.8155 to 33.82. The RMSE results were from 1.027 to 40.86. And lastly, the hybrid ensemble model achieved high R2 scores across the three stocks with range from 0.9304 to 0.9601. These findings highlight the effectiveness and robustness of the hybrid ensemble approach in stock price forecasting.
Keywords: Stock Price Forecasting, Hybrid Ensemble Models, LSTM, Random Forest, ARIMA, Meta-Learning, Financial Time Series

Title: Stocks and models: A comparative benchmark of machine learning and deep learning approaches for stock market prediction
Authors: William and Abraham Kefas Wilham and Sonya Rapinta Manalu
Abstract: The stock market, a cornerstone of global finance, plays a critical role in connecting investors with companies seeking capital through Initial Public Offerings (IPOs). Despite its opportunities for wealth generation, the market’s inherent volatility and com- plexity pose significant challenges for accurate prediction. To address these limitations, this study explores the growing impact of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) in stock market forecasting. The findings aim to inform investors, researchers, and practitioners in selecting effective tools for financial forecasting amidst the uncertainties of the stock market. This paper benchmark the performance of three prominent time-series models such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) by using 76203 dataset of historical OHLCV (Open, High, Low, Close, Volume) stock data. This study finds that while XGBoost offers the fastest training and inference times, LSTM consistently outperforms both GRU and XGBoost in terms of forecasting accuracy compared to GRU and XGBoost. Specifically, XGBoost achieves lower error values across key metrics such as RSME, MAE, MAPE, and higher R² scores, though the differences among the models remain relatively close.
Keywords: Stock Market Prediction, Stock Prediction Algorithm, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Comparative Benchmark

Title: Multimodal Financial Sentiment for Stock Return Prediction
Authors: Petr Hajek and Josef Novotny and Michal Munk and Dasa Munkova
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel multimodal deep learning framework for stock return prediction that integrates heterogeneous data sources: technical indicators, market investor sentiment indices, and textual sentiment extracted from earnings conference call transcripts. The proposed model employs a hybrid architecture combining transformer encoder for the technical modality and neural networks for market and textual modalities. A modality-level attention mechanism is used in a late fusion setup to dynamically weight the contributions of each modality. We evaluate our model on a large-scale dataset comprising 24,821 samples from 497 S&P 500 companies over the period 2010–2022. The results show that our model outperforms traditional models (LSTM, BiL-STM, CNN-LSTM) and alternative fusion strategies, achieving a directional accuracy of 59.94% on the test set. Attention weight analysis confirms that all three modalities contribute meaningfully to prediction performance. These results demonstrate the overall effectiveness of the proposed framework in accurately predicting abnormal stock returns in a multimodal setting.
Keywords: Multimodal fusion, Financial sentiment, Stock market, Prediction, Earnings conference calls

Title: A Hybrid ML Algorithm Trading Model combining Sentiment, Technical Indicator and Risk Management
Authors: Sacheen Shrestha and Cesar Sanin and Mehedi Hasan and Sebastian Ramirez V and Edward Szczerbicki
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) and sentiment-aware machine learning are examples of technological developments that have influenced algorithmic trading using non-traditional data sources such as social media. The unpredictable, non-stationary nature of financial data makes stock market prediction difficult. Machine learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for dynamic market adaptation. The machine learning model’s ability to reduce trading risk and maximise profits has been limited by the current methodologies’ frequent lack of regard for structured risk management. In this paper, we propose a hybrid model combining sentiment analysis and technical indicators along with market data to predict the trend in the market. We also explore the returns obtained from the model and compare them with our risk strategy and traditional buy-and-hold (B&H) strategy. The results show that machine learning can decisively outperform traditional methods if paired with efficient risk management, which contributes to our understanding of machine learning-driven trading.
Keywords: Algorithmic Trading, Machine Learning, Sentiment Analysis, Volatility indicators

Title: A Comprehensive Comparison of Deep Learning Models for Forecasting Developing Market Indices: Evidence from the Vietnamese Stock Market
Authors: Hoang Huu Son and Nghiem Thi Phuong and Nguyen Thuy Linh and Phung Thanh Loan
Abstract: Forecasting stock markets in emerging and frontier economies is challenging due to volatility and nonlinear behavior. Although deep learning has advanced financial forecasting, most existing studies focus on mature markets, leaving little evidence for developing contexts. This paper examines the performance of four architectures in predicting the VN-Index: Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional (Bi-LSTM) and Transformer. The results indicate that Transformer models provide the best accuracy for short-term forecasts, while Bi-LSTM performance best over medium and longer horizons. Models with 256 hidden units achieve the most effective balance, outperforming smaller configurations while matching the accuracy of larger ones. Forecasting reliability further improves with sliding windows of 8-11 weeks. These findings reflect the structural characteristics of frontier markets and offer practical guidance for applying deep learning methods in developing stock markets.
Keywords: Fontier Stock Market, VNINDEX, MLP, LSTM, Bi-LSTM, Transformer

Title: Enhancing Stock Market Prediction with Temporal Graph Neural Networks and Large Language Model-Based Explainability
Authors: Tianye Wang
Abstract: Interpreting deep learning predictions in financial markets remains a central challenge, as temporal dependencies and inter-stock relations often obscure model reasoning. This paper introduces a unified framework that combines Temporal Graph Convolutional Network for stPGExpla for grapLarge Language Models (LLMs) such as GPT-4o and LLaMA3 to translate structural explanations into natural-language financial reports. Experiments on the S&P 100 and NASDAQ-100 benchmarks show that TGCNs capture spatiotemporal dependencies effectively, achieving test accuracies of 58.9% and 50.6%, respectively. To assess explanation quality, we propose a factual sensitivity protocol and find that GPT-4o generates the most consistent and context-sensitive reports. While predictive accuracy remains moderate due to market volatility, the primary contribution lies in improving model transparency and accessibility, bridging complex GNN outputs with human-readable narratives. The study also outlines directions for future work, including real-time deployment and user-in-the-loop evaluation to better align explainable AI with financial practice.
Keywords: Temporal Graph Convolutional Networks, Explainable AI, Large Language Models, Stock Trend Forecasting, Financial Analysis Report

Title: StockMARL: A Novel Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning System to Dynamically Improve Trading Strategies
Authors: Peiyan Zou and Peer-Olaf Siebers
Abstract: Contemporary financial markets, shaped by geopolitical tensions, technological innovation, and economic shocks, require adaptive trading strategies. We propose a novel framework that integrates multi-agent simulation with Reinforcement Learning (RL), allowing RL agents to acquire trading strategies by observing heterogeneous rule-based and reactive agents that emulate real-world investor behaviors such as day trading, momentum chasing, and risk aversion. To evaluate this approach, we introduce Stock-MARL, a multi-agent RL stock market simulation platform. Experimental results show that our observational diversity learning approach has advantages compared to models trained on historical price data and other MARL methods, with RL agents effectively deriving resilient strategies by learning from diverse reactive agent behaviors.
Keywords: stock markets, portfolio optimization, trading strategies, multi-agent simulation, reinforcement learning

Title: Machine Learning-based Financial Market Volatility Prediction Models
Authors: Peining Liu
Abstract: Aiming at the problem that traditional technical analysis is difficult to accurately capture the non-linear fluctuation of stock prices, this paper takes stock 300059 as the research object, and based on the historical trading data from 1st April to 30th August, 2025, constructs the Random Forest Dual Model (Classification model predicts the direction of upward and downward movement, and Regression model predicts the closing price) and the multi-dimensional technical indicators such as moving average line, price fluctuation and RSI are extracted as input. The feature correlation is verified through visual analysis, and the model is compared with linear regression and support vector regression. The results show that the random forest regression model has MAE of 0.194, MSE of 0.088, an R2 of 0.981, and a classification model accuracy of 91.8%, which is significantly better than the comparative model; the feature importance analysis shows that the closing price and the intraday high and low prices contribute the most.
Keywords: Stock price prediction, Random forest, Dual model, Technical indicators, Comparison of model performance, Significance of features

Title: Enhancing Stock Market Forecasting in Emerging African Markets:A Multimodal Approach Integrating Sentiment Analysis and Technical Indicators Using Deep Learning
Authors: Bilal Azdine and Anouar Hasbaoui and Mounime Elkabbouri and Tariq Rachid and Marouane Kamal and Abdallah Abarda
Abstract: This study investigates the contribution of deep learning-based Natural Language Processing (NLP) and sentiment analysis to the forecasting of the Moroccan MSI 20 stock index. Unlike previous research focused on developed markets, this work introduces a multimodal architecture tailored for volatile emerging African contexts. Grounded in behavioral finance, our approach combines FinBERT-derived news sentiments with deep learning models (LSTM, GRU, and ANN) enriched by technical indicators such as RSI, %K, and %R. Empirical results on MSI 20 data (2020-2024) show improved prediction accuracy, with GRU achieving an R2 of 0.65 in daily forecasts. This approach challenges the Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH) by quantifying emotional biases in volatile African markets, providing practical insights for investment strategies amid globalization and digitalization. The findings underscore the potential of AI-driven tools for African financial institutions to mitigate risks and optimize decision-making.
Keywords: Stock market forecasting, Sentiment analysis, Deep learning, Technical indicators, Emerging African markets, FinBERT, Behavioral finance

Title: Transformer Deep Learning Model for Regional Economic Forecasting
Authors: Jing Shan
Abstract: Regional economic forecasting is an important basis for formulating macroeconomic policies and micro investment decisions. Traditional econometric models and classical machine learning methods have limitations in dealing with high-dimensional, nonlinear, and long-term dependent economic time series data. This study explores the application of Transformer deep learning models in multi indicator prediction of regional economy. By constructing an encoder decoder architecture that combines temporal feature embedding and positional encoding, the model can effectively capture the complex dynamic correlations and long-term dependencies between regional economic indicators. This study selects multidimensional monthly economic data of a Chinese urban agglomeration (such as GDP, fixed assets investment, total retail sales of social consumer goods, total imports and exports, industrial electricity consumption, etc.) for empirical analysis. The experimental results show that the proposed Transformer model has significantly better predictive performance than baseline models such as seasonal autoregressive moving average model, Prophet model, and long short-term memory network in multiple evaluation indicators. The contribution of this study is to provide a new and more powerful deep learning tool for regional economic forecasting, and to verify its effectiveness in capturing complex economic dynamics, which has practical significance for improving the intelligence level of regional economic monitoring and early warning.
Keywords: Transformer, Regional economic forecasting, Deep learning, Time series prediction, Attention mechanism

Title: Evolutionary Neural Architecture Search for Early Sepsis Prediction in Clinical Time Series
Authors: Amrithkala M Shetty and Kishore S and Rekha R Nair and Tina babu and Praveen N
Abstract: The automation of architecture design provided by Neural Architecture Search (NAS) presents a promising solution; however, traditional approaches are prohibitively expensive and do not handle issues unique to the healthcare industry, such as irregular sampling, missing values, and heterogeneous feature importance. The effective Evolutionary Neural Architecture Search (ENAS) framework designed for clinical time series prediction is presented in this paper. The approach uses evolutionary strategies to explore the architecture space and incorporates domain-specific constraints and methods for optimization to minimize computational overhead. Within the key innovations are a new evolutionary search strategy, a progressive training regime for efficient resource allocation, and a performance-aware evaluation framework that balances predictive accuracy and computational efficiency. When tested on the PhysioNet Challenge 2019 dataset for early sepsis prediction, the framework performs better than baseline models, with an AUROC of 0.857 and an AUPRC of 0.531. Additionally, it attains faster inference times while utilizing fewer parameters. The results show that the framework can identify high-performing architectures with significantly less processing power than traditional NAS methods. This work supports the use of automated machine learning systems in resource-constrained clinical settings by improving early detection capabilities and clinical interpretability. The efficacy of ENAS in predicting sepsis points to wider applicability to other medical tasks that call for reliable and effective temporal data analysis.
Keywords: Neural Architecture Search (NAS), Evolutionary Algorithms, Clinical Time Series, Sepsis Prediction, Automated Machine Learning, Healthcare AI

Title: A Deep Learning Method for Stock Investment Based on Neural Network Data Mining Technology
Authors: Juan Wang and Ran Teng
Abstract: With the progression of China’s economy, the stock market is playing a more significantt role as a "barometer" of the macro-economy, but relatively speaking, China’s stock market is still relatively young, the development time is relatively short, the influencing factors are complex, speculation is very strong, and the risks it faces are greater.This not only tests the professional judgment ability of investors, but also puts forward higher requirements for the scientificity of market supervision and analysis methods. There are many ways to study the price trend of the stock market. If we can choose a good method to study and predict the price trend and bring investors the basis for investment, we can reduce the investment risk.Both the experience accumulation of traditional analysis methods and the technological breakthrough of machine learning methods provide important support for the research on stock market. This paper mainly compares and analyzes the traditional stock analysis methods and machine learning methods, and strives to choose the appropriate method to guide investors to invest rationally and propel the healthy progress of China’s securities market.
Keywords: machine learning, data mining, neural network

Title: Adaptive Ensemble Learning for Financial Risk Assessment and Real-Time Investment Decision Support
Authors: Tina Babu and Rekha R Nair and Mano Shankari J
Abstract: Financial markets have become increasingly volatile due to macroeconomic uncertainties, geopolitical disruptions, and rapid technological change, necessitating more robust and adaptive risk assessment models. This study presents a novel multi-level ensemble learning framework that integrates five distinct base learners—Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Machine, Support Vector Machine, Long Short-Term Memory, and Extreme Learning Machine—into a stacked meta-architecture. A dynamic meta-learner adaptively reweights models in real-time based on prediction error minimization, while volatility is estimated using ensemble-augmented GARCH. Additionally, a constrained portfolio optimization module balances return, variance, and Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) for investment decisions. Evaluated using a large-scale dataset comprising 127 FRED indicators and ETF market data, the proposed system achieved a 94.7% accuracy, an annualized return of 18.6% and a Sharpe ratio of 2.34. These results significantly outperform existing methods such as LSTM-only models (91.2% accuracy, Sharpe 2.12) and the Black-Litterman framework (76.3% accuracy, Sharpe 1.12).This framework not only improves financial forecasting but also enhances societal resilience by supporting more informed, timely, and risk-aware investment strategies, benefiting both institutional and retail investors.
Keywords: Financial Risk Modeling, Ensemble Learning, Investment Decision Support, Adaptive Weighting, Portfolio Optimization

Title: Intelligent Market Forecasting Using AI Models: Case Study on Stocks and Cryptocurrencies
Authors: Al Naabi W.; Dharmalingam R.
Abstract: The research work addresses the challenges investors face in tracking and analyzing financial markets, stocks, and cryptocurrencies by developing an advanced price prediction platform. Many existing platforms lack comprehensive solutions, such as precise real-time data, dynamic notifications, and sophisticated analytical tools, limiting users' ability to make informed investment decisions and respond effectively to market changes. This research focuses on creating a complete web-based platform that uses AI models, including linear regression, LSTM, and RNN, to predict market prices based on key parameters such as the opening price, the highest price, the lowest price, and the volume of trades. The front-end is built with HTML5, CSS and JavaScript, and the back-end uses Python with Flask. Real-time data integration is achieved through APIs like'Yahoo Finance' and'Finnhub', which provide customization alerts and interactive analytics tools to track trends and forecast market movements. In a 7-year dataset covering AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN and BTC, the best models achieved strong out-of-sample precision: for Apple (AAPL) R2=0.98 and RMSE=$1.42; for Amazon (AMZN) RMSE=$1.06 (lowest); for Google (GOOGL) R2=0.78 (moderate fit); and for Microsoft (MSFT) RMSE=$1.62 (good fit). The authors release a three-tier reference architecture and show that the platform delivers stable, real-time operation with precise alerting underload. Comparative analysis against recent literature indicates our results are competitive with modern deep learning baselines, while emphasizing a production-ready design. © 2026 The Authors.
Keywords: AI based Stock Price Prediction; Investment Decision Support; Predictive Analytics; Commerce; Costs; Data integration; Decision support systems; Deep learning; Electronic trading; Financial markets; Information use; Investments; Market Research; Prediction models; AI based stock price prediction; Case-studies; Decision supports; Google+; Investment decision support; Investment decisions; Market forecasting; MicroSoft; Real-time data; Stock price prediction; Predictive analytics

Title: Hybrid Recurrent Expert Gating: An Adaptive Mixture of Experts Framework for Financial Time Series Prediction
Authors: Vandita Pandey and Manish Pandey and Yadunath Pathak and Rahul Haripriya
Abstract: This study introduces an Adaptive Mixture of Experts (MoE) framework for stock price prediction, combining Long Short Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) architectures to address the challenges of nonstationary financial time series. Using daily OHLCV (Open, High, Low, Close, Volume) data for Alphabet Inc. (GOOGLE) from January 1, 2021 to August 5, 2025, the model dynamically allocates expert contributions through a learnable softmax gating mechanism, enhancing robustness across trending, volatile, stable regimes. Compared with the strongest single model baseline (GRU), the proposed Adaptive MoE achieves notable reductions in the test set 5.83% in Mean Absolute Error (MAE), 7.47% in Mean Squared Error (MSE), and 3.81% in Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) along with a 0.94% improvement in Coefficient of Determination (R2). Similar gains are observed in the training set, confirming a stable generalization. Analysis of gating weights reveals interpretable attributions, with GRU favored in general, LSTM activated under long memory dynamics, and RNN under short horizon conditions. In general, the framework provides a scalable, interpretable, and computationally efficient approach to financial forecasting, and can be extended with sparse routing and additional expert families for broader applicability across assets and horizons.
Keywords: Hybrid deep learning, Adaptive Mixture of Experts, RNN, LSTM, GRU, Stock Market Prediction, Regime switching, Gating network

Title: Synergy in Forecasting: A Comparative Study of Hybrid Transformer based Ensembles for Stock Market Prediction
Authors: Ravi Ranjan and Kapil Sharma and Akshi Kumar
Abstract: Analysing financial markets is an important process to empower investment decision-making and help ensure people can make the best opportunities without losing money while waiting for positive returns. Financial markets generally consist of an ecosystem of buying and selling securities, and, as a result, financial markets can be an overwhelming and often unsteady experience, especially for those not astute in finance. The unpredictability of the market further complicates the analysis of the market. The effort to forecast prices has garnered significant interest in academia and amongst investors and financial institutions. However, the endeavour faces significant obstacles. Ensemble models excel by capturing intricate relationships among the predictions of their component models, typically leading to enhanced accuracy beyond what any single model can achieve. This study proposes two hybrid ensemble architectures combining Transformers with traditional statistical models for stock market forecasting. The first ensemble uses stacking with Transformer and Lasso Regression, while the second uses a weighted combination of Transformer and ARIMAX. Experiments were conducted on two U.S. stocks, AAL and AAME, using eleven years (2013–2023) of daily market data. Evaluation with MSE, RMSE, MAE, and MAPE demonstrates that the Transformer–ARIMAX ensemble reduced prediction errors compared to baseline models, achieving an MSE of 0.003 on AAME and 0.063 on AAL. These results confirm that hybrid ensembles leveraging deep learning and statistical modelling achieve more accurate and robust forecasts than individual models.
Keywords: Financial Forecasting, Time Series Analysis, Hybrid Models, Deep Learning, Machine Learning, Transformer Model

Title: An Informer-Based Real-Time Forecasting with Inverse Scaling Optimization and Bayesian Hyper-parameter Tuning
Authors: Ajit Mohan Pattnayak and Biswajit Sahoo and Aleena Swetapadma
Abstract: This work presents a sophisticated real-time forecasting system for stock price prediction, anchored in a refined Informer-based deep learning framework. Distinct from traditional transformer architectures, the proposed model introduces a novel inverse scaling-aware decoding strategy, designed to enhance interpretability and capture subtle temporal fluctuations inherent in high-frequency financial data. By coupling this with a principled Bayesian optimization pipeline implemented via the Optuna framework, fine-grained tuning of critical hyperparameters has been performed, including sequence length, model depth, forecast horizon, and learning rate. This results in substantial gains in model stability, generalization, and accuracy. The end-to-end pipeline is engineered as a deployable real-time forecasting service. It seamlessly integrates live market data acquisition through the Yahoo Finance API, efficient model inference using PyTorch Lightning, and interactive visual output generation. Empirical evaluation reveals the model’s superiority, achieving an RMSE of 39.68 and an exceptionally low MAPE of 0.14%. Moreover, the framework effectively resolves common challenges in financial prediction tasks, such as negative R² values during periods of heightened volatility. The results validate the Informer’s exceptional capability in modeling long-range dependencies within non-stationary time series and demonstrate the efficacy of inverse scaling coupled with intelligent hyperparameter search. The system sets a precedent for deploying scalable, interpretable, and high-precision forecasting tools in real-world financial ecosystems.
Keywords: Stock Price Prediction, Informer Architecture, Transformer Models, Bayesian Optimization, Optuna, Nifty Index

Title: RNN-based stock price forecasting through the integration of technical indicators, fundamental data, and news sentiment analysis
Authors: Gagatsatya Adiatmaja and Rarasmaya Indraswari and Rika Rokhana and Wiwiet Herulambang
Abstract: Accurately predicting stock prices is vital for making informed investment decisions in capital markets. Stock price volatility is influenced by a range of factors, such as global economic trends, monetary policy shifts, and overall market sentiment. This research proposes a stock price forecasting model utilizing deep learning techniques based on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN). The model integrates three key types of stock price analysis: technical indicators, fundamental financial data, and sentiment analysis from financial news. The study focuses on three prominent Indonesian blue-chip stocks which are components of the LQ45 and IDX30 indices: Bank BCA (BBCA), Astra International (ASII), and Telkom Indonesia (TLKM). The used technical indicator includes moving averages and trading volume, while the fundamental analysis is obtained from annual financial ratios. Sentiment analysis is performed using IndoBERT on articles from the detik.com news portal. The combination of features from those three analyses enhances the accuracy of the stock price forecasting. Among the compared models, Bi-LSTM and Bi-GRU yielded the best results, with Bi-LSTM showing the lowest RMSE for TLKM (65.2) and ASII (119.49), while Bi-GRU showed the lowest RMSE for BBCA (97.79). The findings demonstrate the potential of integrated deep learning approaches to improve the precision and reliability of stock price prediction.
Keywords: Stock price prediction, Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), technical analysis, fundamental analysis, news sentiment analysis

Title: Network-Aware Financial Distress Prediction via Hierarchical Attention on Dynamic Heterogeneous Corporate Networks
Authors: Zhengqi Sun and Fei Shao and Fan Meng
Abstract: Financial distress prediction can benefit from inter-firm relationships such as guarantees, equity linkages, and market co-movements. Most existing models, however, treat firms as independent samples and therefore ignore network structure. We construct a dynamic heterogeneous corporate network with seven relation types for 3,797 Chinese A-share listed companies over 2010–2024 and study one-year-ahead distress prediction, where distress is defined as negative net profit in year t + 1. Our empirical analysis shows that firms in the highest neighbour-distress quintile have a distress rate 3.8× higher than firms in the lowest quintile, including among currently profitable firms. Logistic regressions with year fixed effects further indicate that market-correlation (OR=1.245) and industry (OR=1.137) exposure variables remain significant (p < 0.001) after accounting for firm-level financial characteristics. To model these signals, we propose RA-HTGNN, a Relation-Attention Temporal Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network that combines relation-specific graph convolution, relation-level attention, and GRU-based temporal encoding. A held-out stacking ensemble that combines RA-HTGNN with a Random Forest through a validation-trained meta-learner achieves AUC=0.839. Although standalone RA-HTGNN does not outperform the strongest tabular baseline, it contributes complementary signal that improves ensemble performance; ablations further show that sparse guarantee edges yield the strongest standalone GNN performance, whereas dense market-correlation edges contribute most through ensemble fusion.
Keywords: financial distress prediction, heterogeneous graph neural network, temporal attention, guarantee network, corporate network dependence

Title: Forecasting crude oil futures prices using Bagging Large Language Model
Authors: Kaijian He and Haoran Zhang and Lean Yu and Yingchao Zou
Abstract: In this paper, a new crude oil futures price forecasting model has been proposed to leverage the power of Large Language Model through the bagging ensemble methods. The Bagging LLM based crude oil futures price forecasting model employs the mainstream large language models such as Llama, GPT and OPT as the foundation to construct more effective forecasting algorithms. It can take advantage of the big data encoded in the Large Language Model. LLM is finetuned with the crude oil futures price time series data so that the LLM is adapted to the crude oil forecasting task and can better exploit the pre-trained knowledge in mainstream LLM for the forecasting problem. Comprehensive empirical evaluations using INE crude oil futures price have been conducted and results show the positive performance improvement with the introduction of Large Language Models. This paper finds that the LLMs need to be fully fine-tuned to model the time series characteristics. Furthermore, the Bagging method is used to aggregate forecasts from LLMs applied to bootstrapped datasets to improve the generalization of the model.
Keywords: Crude oil futures price forecasting, Large language model, Bagging algorithm, Fine-tuning algorithm

Title: Economic policy uncertainty as an indicator of abrupt movements in the US stock market
Authors: Tzika P.; Pantelidis T.
Venue: Quarterly Review of Economics and Finance
Abstract: A two regime switching model is developed in an attempt to relate expected US stock market returns to deviations from fundamentals and to Economic Policy Uncertainty (EPU). The analysis is based on monthly data that cover the period from January 1900 to October 2022 and the EPU index is used as an explanatory variable. The findings suggest that the US stock market spends most of the time in a low-volatility regime, periodically switching to a high-volatility regime during times of financial instability. In an attempt to examine the forecasting ability of the model, out-of-sample probabilities of a crash and a boom are estimated recursively. The results provide evidence that our model is able to depict periods of abrupt movements in the US stock market. Finally, the estimated model and the associated probability of a crash are used to develop and evaluate a proposed trading strategy, in order to analyse the financial usefulness of the model. A simple simulation reveals that our trading rule produces statistically significant abnormal returns and manages to outperform the simple buy-and-hold strategy for the period before the Covid-19 crisis. © 2024 Board of Trustees of the University of Illinois
Keywords: Economic policy uncertainty; Regime switching model; Stock market

Title: Energy-related uncertainty and international stock market volatility
Authors: Salisu A.A.; Ogbonna A.E.; Gupta R.; Bouri E.
Venue: Quarterly Review of Economics and Finance
Abstract: This paper predicts the daily return volatility of 28 advanced and developing stock markets using monthly metrics of the corresponding country and global energy-related uncertainty indexes (EUIs) recently proposed in the literature. Using data in their “natural” frequencies to avoid aggregation bias, the results show that country-specific and global EUIs have predictive powers for stock returns volatility for the in-sample periods, with increased levels of EUIs exhibiting the tendency to heighten volatility. This predictability also withstands various out-of-sample forecast horizons, implying that EUI is a statistically relevant predictor in the out-of-sample analysis. The forecast precision of the GARCH-MIDAS model is improved by incorporating global EUIs relatively more than country-specific EUIs. The robustness of the findings with respect to the choice of EUI and sample definition is further confirmed. The outcomes have important policy implications for the concerned stakeholders who are concerned with stability in the global financial system and economy. © 2024 The Authors
Keywords: Daily stock returns volatility; Developed and developing economies; GARCH-MIDAS; Monthly energy-related uncertainty index; Predictions

Title: Mitigating downside risk: ESG integration in portfolio construction with stock preselection using machine learning and mean-CVaR optimization
Authors: Larry Van Wallendael and Line Vanneste and Yanyi Zhang and Alexander Stevens and Johannes De Smedt
Venue: The Quarterly Review of Economics and Finance
Abstract: Recent studies indicate that Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors are valuable indicators of downside risk. However, research into how ESG integration within portfolio construction can reduce extreme investment risks is limited. This study investigates ESG integration for downside risk mitigation within a dual-phase framework comprising stock preselection and portfolio optimization. ESG scores are incorporated either linearly in actual returns or through negative screening. We utilize various machine learning techniques for stock preselection, followed by mean Conditional Value-at-Risk optimization in the portfolio phase. Our analysis includes both in-sample and out-of-sample testing across periods characterized by low and high market volatility. Results indicate that ESG-informed returns effectively mitigate portfolio downside risk, particularly during volatile periods, while ESG integration through screening proves less effective. Overall, this study contributes novel insights into the nuanced effects of ESG integration strategies on portfolio downside risk management.
Keywords: ESG integration, Portfolio construction, Portfolio optimization, Downside risk management, Conditional value at risk (CVaR), Mean conditional value at risk (mean-CVaR), Machine learning

Title: Forecasting firm valuation through investor sentiments: A machine learning-based redefinition in China
Authors: Ul Abideen Z.; Wu K.
Venue: Quarterly Review of Economics and Finance
Abstract: China’s dynamic stock market, characterized by high volatility and significant government intervention, provides a unique setting for examining how investor sentiment affects firm value. This study examines the effects of optimistic, pessimistic, and neutral sentiments on firm value in China’s A-share market from 2018 to 2024. Employing machine learning and econometric techniques, the research rigorously examines how these sentiments drive valuation dynamics. Findings reveal that optimistic sentiment significantly increases firm value, particularly in high-profitability sectors, increasing financial resilience. In contrast, pessimistic sentiment depresses firm value, highlighting the adverse impact of negative perceptions on market capitalization. Neutral sentiment, while less pronounced, promotes stability during periods of market uncertainty. In a cross- market comparison with the U.S. using StockTwits data, all four sentiment dimensions exhibit stronger effects in China, with the largest amplification for pessimistic sentiment ((Formula presented) ), followed by optimistic ((Formula presented) ), overall ((Formula presented) ), and neutral ((Formula presented) ). Title: Quantile-transformed multi-attention residual framework (QT-MARF) for medium-term PV and wind power prediction
Authors: Adeel Feroz Mirza and Zhaokun Shu and Muhammad Usman and Majad Mansoor and Qiang Ling
Abstract: The increasing generation of renewable electrical power, particularly from wind and solar sources, has significantly influenced the national energy and power transmission systems. However, accurate forecasting of wind and photovoltaic (PV) power remains challenging due to the stochastic and highly nonlinear nature of wind speed and solar irradiance. Traditional models often fail to produce accurate power forecasts. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel deep learning model based on the Quantile-Transformed Multi-Attention Residual Framework (QT-MARF). The proposed model is built on a Transformer architecture with Residual Net and Multi-Head Attention. QT-MARF utilizes sequential processing through gated residual networks, enabling the model to learn complex patterns and make accurate power forecasts. The model utilizes PV and wind data from Natal, Santa Vitoria, and the Chinese State Grid (CSG). Case studies are conducted to validate the estimation performance of the hybrid models. The proposed QT-MARF demonstrates promising results in terms of accuracy and efficiency, outperforming traditional models in metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), correlation coefficient (CC), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and R-squared (R2). Comparative analysis with state-of-the-art techniques such as the Inception-embedded attention-based memory fully-connected network (IAMFN) model, CNN-GRU, CNN-LSTM, and RNN highlights the superiority of the proposed model. These findings suggest that the proposed model offers a promising solution for the challenging task of wind and PV power forecasting.

Title: Renewable energy stock prices forecast using environmental television newscasts investors’ sentiment
Authors: Loutfi A.A.
Abstract: The world is turning towards renewable energies to sustainably meet its increasing demand for energy. Naturally, this is being accompanied by a strong momentum in trading within the renewable energy market. Today, behavioral finance acknowledges the major role of wider psychological and social factors in shaping the stock market, through influencing investors' sentiment. Therefore, this paper explores the understudied question of whether environmental television newscasts can be used as a proxy for measuring investors' sentiment and in helping to improve the forecast accuracy of renewable energy stock prices. First, we compute the sentiment scores of the environmental newscasts of CNN, BBC News, MSNBC, and Fox News. We then use machine learning to implement a baseline forecast model, as well as an augmented one which takes the newscasts’ sentiment scores as input. Using four different accuracy metrics, we find that environmental TV newscasts can improve the forecast accuracy of renewable energy stock prices in 78 % of the experiments, and decrease the Mean Absolute Error, Mean Squared Error, and Root Mean Squared Error in 83.3 % of the experiments. We also find that the sentiments of conservative news outlets, such as Fox News, can improve the forecast accuracy of renewable energy stock prices more than liberal ones. Finally, we provide some insights into potential psychological dynamics that can help us make sense of the results, such as the negativity bias theory. © 2024 The Author

Title: Joint interval forecasting of renewable energy stocks using a secondary decomposition approach
Authors: Shuihan Liu and Yunjie Wei and Pan Peng and Shouyang Wang
Abstract: Upon the climate change and energy transition, the renewable energy market has emerged as a new investment hotspot. Recognizing the importance of precise stock price interval forecasting for strategic planning and investment decisions, this paper introduces a novel framework that employs a two-stage decomposition and joint prediction approach for interval forecasting of multiple renewable energy stocks. By treating multiple stocks as a single Multi-Interval Time Series (MITS), our method captures inter-stock correlations and market dynamics. Initially, stocks are decomposed using the Multivariate Empirical Mode Decomposition (MEMD) algorithm, following a secondary decomposition of complex components using Multivariate Variational Mode Decomposition (MVMD) based on the complexity and noise present in the initial decomposition. Each frequency component, enriched with inter-stock information, is then predicted and integrated to yield final interval predictions. This approach leverages the inherent interdependencies among the stocks and optimizes the decomposition structure of sub-problems, resulting in superior predictive performance compared to traditional single-stock and decomposition-ensemble prediction models. In the specific empirical analysis, four representative stocks from the sustainable energy sector are selected to generate interval forecasts. The error metrics and statistical tests indicate that our proposed method outperforms other benchmark models and demonstrates strong robustness.

Title: Efficient calculation of distributed photovoltaic power generation power prediction via deep learning
Authors: Jiaqian Li and Congjun Rao and Mingyun Gao and Xinping Xiao and Mark Goh
Abstract: Distributed photovoltaic (PV) power generation has gained significant support from national policies and has seen rapid development due to its ability to adapt to local conditions, its cleanliness and efficiency, as well as its notable environmental and economic benefits. However, PV power generation is highly susceptible to fluctuations and unpredictability caused by varying weather conditions. Accurate prediction of PV power generation is essential for maintaining grid stability and efficient operation. To improve prediction accuracy, we propose a novel model, PerfCNN-LSTM, which combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a long short-term memory (LSTM) network with the Performer self-attention mechanism. This model aims to enhance PV power generation forecasting. By extracting local features from the data, the model further captures global features through the integration of the Performer self-attention mechanism layer. This layer introduces linear random feature mapping, transforming the originally nonlinear attention weight calculation into linear attention, which simplifies the attention process and reduces the model's computational complexity. The output from the Performer layer is directly fed into the LSTM model to generate the final PV power generation prediction. We evaluated the performance of the model across three different datasets using key metrics such as MAE, RMSE, MSE, and R2. When compared with six other deep learning models, the PerfCNN-LSTM demonstrates superior prediction accuracy.
Keywords: Distributed photovoltaic power generation, Performer self-attention mechanism, Deep learning, PerfCNN-LSTM model

Title: Predicting renewable energy stock volatility: A GARCH-CNN approach with indicator analysis
Authors: Kim S.; An J.; Yang J.-S.
Abstract: The renewable energy (RE) stock market is experiencing rapid growth, driven by environmentally conscious investors seeking to support a greener future while pursuing profitable opportunities. This study aims to forecast RE stock volatility, which is critical for managing risks in the RE stock market. We employ a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model combined with Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroscedasticity (GARCH) forecasts to predict RE stock volatility. Three groups of indicators – internal stock, financial market, and policy uncertainty – are incorporated as additional inputs. The results demonstrate that integrating internal stock and financial market indicators significantly reduces prediction errors compared to the traditional GARCH model. Conversely, models incorporating the policy uncertainty indicator produce higher errors, suggesting that these indicators may introduce noise. SHapely Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identifies the internal stock indicator, particularly the squared log returns of RE stocks, as a dominant factor, with the financial market indicator serving as a complementary factor. By integrating deep learning with econometric models, this study enhances the prediction of RE stock volatility and underscores the importance of selecting appropriate indicators. The findings provide valuable insights for investors and policymakers seeking to better understand and manage RE investment risks, highlighting the key drivers of RE stock volatility. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A novel computer vision-based approach for autonomous building facade material stock estimation
Authors: Rajaratnam D.; Stewart R.A.; Liu T.; Vieira A.S.
Abstract: Estimating building stock at the elemental level is essential for a circular economy. However, the lack of information on building stock due to considerable time and costs associated with data collection poses a significant challenge in large-scale analysis. This study employed computer vision-based façade classification and weighted material intensity to estimate building façade material stock using a bottom-up approach. Autonomous semantic enhancements on façade material typologies and opening areas aided better estimation of building-facing materials’ weight. ResNet 50 deep learning architecture was chosen, with an F1 score of 0.77 and 80 % accuracy. Most façade classes have achieved a relatively high level of accuracy of predictions. “Common Brick”, “Face Brick”, “Concrete Blocks”, and “Concrete” were identified as the most widespread façade materials in the model deployed area of interest: Southport (SA3), City of Gold Coast, Australia. The model provides the necessary foundations for progressing circular economy and urban metabolism efforts. © 2025 The Author(s)

Title: Feeling the heat? Analyzing climate change sentiment in Spain using Twitter data
Authors: Maria L. Loureiro and Maria Alló
Abstract: To shed light on the recent debate about climate change in this post-pandemic scenario, we take advantage of a unique dataset that combines geo-tagged social media data from Twitter in Spain from 2017 to 2022. Twitter conversations have been analyzed with natural language processing techniques to obtain sentiment scores related to climate change. These were merged with additional relevant control variables, aiming to understand the role of the contributing factors on the evolution of the hedonic scores, including external temperatures, the occurrence of heat waves, and deaths related to climate. We find a strong negative effect of external temperatures on sentiment, aggravated by recent increases in the frequency of heat waves and deaths related to climate. Further, this negative sentiment is accentuated after experiencing the recent COVID-19.

Title: Improved prediction of global gold prices: An innovative Hurst-reconfiguration-based machine learning approach
Authors: Mo Yang and Ruotong Wang and Zixun Zeng and Peizhi Li
Abstract: With gold being one of the most important precious metals that play irreplaceable roles in the global market, understanding the future movement of the gold price is of significant importance for investment and risk management worldwide. However, gold prices are subject to volatility and can experience significant fluctuations over time due to economic uncertainty shocks such as the China-US Trade War, Russia-Ukraine war, and COVID-19, which make the forecasting of gold price a challenging task. In this paper, we propose a hybrid forecasting model for gold prices based on the Hurst-oriented reconfiguration and machine learning approach and illustrate its usefulness by analyzing the gold prices of three major markets. We conduct a multifractal analysis of the decomposed series and scrutinize the predictability of each sub-series and its relationship with the Hurst exponent. Empirical results show that there are negative relationships between forecasting error and the Hurst exponent and between the number of embedding dimensions and the Hurst exponent. Our Hurst-based hybrid model outperforms other conventional prediction models in terms of prediction errors and accuracy of direction prediction. The findings of this study shed light on a better understanding of the temporal features of the gold market and provide references for improving investment and hedging strategies.
Keywords: Hurst exponent, Decomposition and ensemble, Gold price forecasting, Swarm intelligence optimization

Title: How do seasonal, significant events, and policies affect China's REE export prices? Based on deep learning perspective
Authors: Qing Guo and Zishan Mai
Abstract: This paper aims to accurately predict China's rare earth export prices and reveal the impact of variables such as seasonality, significant events, finance, and supply and demand on rare earth price volatility. Daily datasets of light and heavy rare earths from 2011 to 2023 were used, and the Tree-structured Parzen Estimator-Temporal Fusion Transformer model was employed to predict rare earth prices. Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise and partial dependence plots were used to reveal the factors affecting price volatility. The following conclusions were drawn: (1) The Tree-structured Parzen Estimator-Temporal Fusion Transformer deep learning model can provide more accurate rare earth price prediction information; (2) Light rare earth prices are more susceptible to cyclical influences, while heavy rare earth prices are more affected by significant events. The outbreak of COVID-19 has had a long-term impact on both light and heavy rare earth prices; (3) The fluctuations in heavy rare earth prices are mainly influenced by financial factors, while the fluctuations in light rare earth prices are influenced by multiple factors such as finance, supply and demand, and macroeconomics; (4) An increase in resource tax rates may lead to a decrease in rare earth prices, while an increase in restrictions on rare earth mining may lead to an increase in rare earth prices.
Keywords: Rare earths, Prices, TFT model, Prediction, Influential factors

Title: A predictive model for the security and stability of the lithium-ion battery industry chain based on price modal combinations
Authors: Li Jian-fei and Peng Han and Luo Xiao-yu
Abstract: Prices act as crucial market signals within industrial chains, and the smooth transmission of prices has significantly impacts on the safety and stability of the entire chain. This paper considers the lithium-ion battery industry chain as a complex system and uses prices as modal signals to construct an FEEMD-NAR-HMM industrial chain safety and stability prediction model. The research findings are as follows: (1) The lithium-ion industry chain exhibits a typical "price-stability" dissipative structure, where the consistency of price fluctuations within the industry chain has a significant impact on its overall safety and stability. (2) When products at different stages of the lithium-ion industry chain experience simultaneous price increases or decreases, the safety and stability of the industry chain are at a high level. When the transmission smoothness of price fluctuations across different stages of the lithium-ion industry chain is low, the safety and stability of the industry chain are at a low level. (3) In the near future, the lithium-ion industry chain will continue to exposed to volatility risks. The government should implement macroeconomic control measures to stabilize the lithium-ion market and increase research investment in lithium resource recycling to prevent a crisis of lithium resource shortages.

Title: The predictive power of the oil variance risk premium
Authors: McMillan D.G.; Ziadat S.A.
Abstract: This paper examines the ability of the oil market variance risk premium (VRP) to predict both financial and key macroeconomic series. Interest in understanding the movement of such variables increasingly involves considering measures of investor risk, for which the VRP, that incorporates both implied and realised variance, has recently come to the fore. It is well established that oil price movement impacts both the stock market and wider economy and thus, we examine whether this is also true of the oil VRP. Using monthly US data over the period from 2009 to 2021, we demonstrate the nature of oil VRP predictive power for oil and stock returns, as well as output growth, unemployment, and inflation. Of notable interest, while predictability from the oil VRP series dominates at the one-month horizon and (largely) wanes at over longer time periods, the reverse is found for the stock VRP. These results are robust to the inclusion of additional, established, predictor variables. This indicates that the impact of oil market risk has a more immediate effect on both the stock market and economy, with stock market risk reflecting longer term considerations. A simple out-of-sample exercise supports the view that the inclusion of oil VRP improves forecasts over alternative models that exclude this series. © 2025 The Authors

Title: Globality in the metal markets: Leveraging cross-learning to forecast aluminum and copper prices
Authors: Oikonomou K.; Damigos D.; Dimitriou D.
Abstract: Over the last 25 years, aluminum and copper prices have fluctuated significantly, impacting mining companies, economies of mining countries and global financial markets. Accurate price forecasting can be useful for better budget planning, strategic decision making and portfolio management. To bridge recent developments in time series forecasting with commodity price forecasting, we investigate the performance of a recently prominent framework called global forecasting or cross-learning. Juxtaposed to the local approach, under which one model would be used for each time series requiring forecasts, this framework involves the training of a single (global) model using a set of relevant time series to create future predictions. In our analysis, we assume that incorporating stock prices of mining companies into global forecasting models can enhance the prediction accuracy of aluminum and copper prices compared to traditional forecasting methods. In this direction, we use a pool of auxiliary time series that includes the prices of the two commodities and the stock prices of major companies involved in their production and processing to train global feed-forward neural networks. The models differ in their approach to selecting relevant time series used in training and are either used as standalones or in combination with standard univariate models to forecast the two commodities’ prices 3, 6 and 12 months ahead. The performance of the models is then compared to benchmark univariate (local) models, namely the naïve method, ARIMA, and autoregressive feed-forward neural networks. The analysis suggests that the incorporation of information from different (albeit related) markets achieved through cross-learning is beneficial for forecasting the prices of the two commodities since, for all forecast horizons examined, the models achieving the lowest out-of-sample error were either standalone global models or local-global ensembles. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Data-driven transformer-based explainable deep learning model for real-time TBM performance prediction
Authors: Ankang Ji and Yiyi Zhu and Hongqin Fan and Xiaolong Xue and Minggong Zhang and Jason Xin Zhou
Abstract: Aiming to effectively and efficiently predict tunnel boring machine (TBM) penetration rates to assist in guiding the operation management, this research proposes TransXTBMNet, a Transformer-based explainable network designed for predicting TBM penetration rates in real-time, which integrates ensemble bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) and improved Transformer to capture the complex interative relationship between operational parameters of TBM and penetration rates, enabling real-time precise predictions. Furthermore, the method encompasses various components: the data preparation process, the SHAP-based model explainability, a loss function, and performance metrics to collectively enhance robust data quality and ensure accurate predictions in dynamic excavation environments. Validation on the real TBM operation dataset demonstrates TransXTBMNet’s exceptional performance, with metrics like Mean Squared Error (MSE) = 0.2529, Root MSE (RMSE) = 0.5029, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) = 0.2991, Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) = 1.4984 %, and R2 = 0.9770. Comparative analysis shows superior results over other state-of-the-art methods such as conventional recurrent architectures (simple RNN (SRNN), GRU, LSTM) and their bidirectional variants (BiSRNN, BiGRU). SHAP analysis reveals that penetration rate at the previous time step, long with thrust groups A and F play crucial roles in predicting penetration rates. Additionally, the proposed method exhibits improved performance when considering the recorded penetration rate data, highlighting its capability to provide a better performance. Overall, the proposed method TransXTBMNet proves to be an effective and efficient solution in predicting TBM performance, providing valuable real-time guidance for optimizing TBM operations.

Title: S&P 500 stock selection using machine learning classifiers: A look into the changing role of factors
Authors: Antonio Caparrini and Javier Arroyo and Jordi Escayola Mansilla
Venue: Research in International Business and Finance
Abstract: This study examines the profitability of using machine learning algorithms to select a subset of stocks over the S&P 500 using factors as features. We use tree-based algorithms: Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost for their white model capabilities, allowing feature importances extraction. We defined a backtest to train the models with recent data and rebalance the portfolio. Despite incurring more risks, the selected assets of the portfolio outperform the index by using machine learning. Furthermore, we show that the feature importance that determines the best-performing assets changes at different times. Such models providing the evolution of the importance of factors can provide profitability insights while keeping explainability.

Title: Technology and automation in financial trading: A bibliometric review
Authors: Rosella Carè and Douglas Cumming
Venue: Research in International Business and Finance
Abstract: In this bibliometric study, the significant transformations in the financial sector brought about by automation and technological advancements from 1984 to 2022 are explored. A total of 863 articles is analyzed, and a consistent upward trajectory in research focused on fast trading technologies and algorithmic strategies is identified. The key findings reveal that the research is grouped into five thematic clusters, ranging from algorithmic trading and machine learning to systemic risks associated with high-frequency trading and the impacts of algorithmic trading on market quality. This study encapsulates the evolving landscape of financial markets, emphasizing emerging trends in cryptocurrencies and machine learning, which will continue to shape future research directions. In conclusion, five macroareas and ten specific future research areas are proposed.

Title: Predicting consumption-wealth ratio changes and stock market returns
Authors: Wang J.; Taylor A.P.
Venue: Research in International Business and Finance
Abstract: We show that the ability of Lettau and Ludvigson's cay ratio to predict stock market returns could be greatly improved when adjustment is made for variations in expected cay ratio changes. We use the present-value identity of Campbell and Mankiw (1989) to derive the appropriate form of the adjustment and model the adjustment using a handful of macroeconomic variables. We find that the expected cay ratio changes vary in a predictable manner. Using our model to adjust cay improves the annual R̄2 values from 4.42% to 9.55% for in-sample prediction of excess market returns, and the out-of-sample pseudo R2 values increase from -1.88% and -1.72% to 2.38% and 3.69% with the first estimations using information up to 1985 and 1990, respectively. The superior performance also exists in medium-term market return predictions. © 2024 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Investor sentiment and market returns: A multi-horizon analysis
Authors: Nguyen H.H.; Ngo V.M.; Pham L.M.; Van Nguyen P.
Venue: Research in International Business and Finance
Abstract: This study explores the relationship between investor sentiment and market return in the stock market, spanning both long-term and short-term horizons. Using a decade-long dataset (2013–2023) from Facebook, comprising around 773,000 curated posts from an initial 900,000, the research employs the Vector Error Correction Model (VECM) to illuminate long-run dynamics, revealing an equilibrium-restoring mechanism post-shocks between investors’ sentiment and Vietnamese stock market index (VNIndex). Short-term insights emerge from logistic and quantile regression analyses, categorizing market returns based on sentiment and elucidating relationships across market return distribution quantiles. The study also applies advanced machine learning algorithms—such as Decision Tree Regression (DTR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Neural Networks (NN), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), Random Forest (RF), and Deep Neural Networks (DNN)—to demonstrate the predictive power of sentiment indices in forecasting abnormal returns on the VNIndex. The results emphasize the paramount influence of investors’ sentiment in terms of its predictive power compared to traditional autoregressive models of past trading data. Distinct patterns arise when comparing the low and high quantiles of returns distribution, with sentiment indicators being more influential at the lower quantiles. In summary, the research underscores the significant role of investor sentiment in the Vietnamese stock market dynamics and highlights the confluence of sentiment analysis and modern machine learning as a promising frontier in financial research. © 2024 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Volatility forecasting and volatility-timing strategies: A machine learning approach
Authors: Chun D.; Cho H.; Ryu D.
Venue: Research in International Business and Finance
Abstract: Recent increases in stock price volatility have generated renewed interest in volatility-timing strategies. Based on high-dimensional models including machine learning, we predict stock market volatility and apply them to improve the performance of volatility-timing portfolios. Using various evaluation methods, we verify that those machine learning models have better prediction performances relative to the standard volatility models. Asset allocation results suggest that volatility-timing portfolios constructed using machine learning models tend to outperform the market, with higher average returns during the volatile market period. Our empirical evidence supports the application of machine learning in the construction of volatility-timing portfolios. © 2025 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Enhancing stock return prediction in the Chinese market: A GAN-based approach
Authors: Wu H.; Wang Q.; Li J.; Deng Z.
Venue: Research in International Business and Finance
Abstract: With the rapid advancement of machine learning technologies, the accuracy of predictive models has seen continuous improvement. In this paper, we aim to apply machine learning models to predict stock market returns and implement factor investment in the Chinese A-share market. We propose a novel GAN model integrating LSTM, attention mechanisms, and CNN to address time-dependence issues and low signal-to-noise ratios more effectively in stock return prediction. Out-of-sample results demonstrate that the proposed GAN model outperforms other benchmark models in terms of predictive performance and exhibits superior generalization capabilities. Furthermore, our analysis of predictor importance highlights the pivotal role of transaction and profitability metrics in predicting returns in the Chinese A-share market. Additionally, when incorporating macroeconomic predictors into the training data, our model demonstrates stability amidst macroeconomic fluctuations. These empirical findings underscore the potential value of the proposed GAN model in the Chinese stock market investment. © 2025 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Prediction of Chinese stock volatility: Harnessing higher-order moments information of stock and futures markets
Authors: Qiao G.; Wang Y.; Liu W.
Venue: Research in International Business and Finance
Abstract: This paper examines the predictive capacity of higher-order moments (skewness and kurtosis) of the Chinese stock index and futures market for the realized volatility of the stock market. Owing to the model uncertainty caused by structural changes, we propose the use of data-driven combination forecasting, namely, the LASSO-weighted average windows method over forecasts of long short-term memory network (LSTM), support vector regression (SVR), or the ordinary least squares (OLS) method. Empirical findings indicate that the LSTM method outperforms both SVR and OLS. The LASSO-weighted forecasts across these three methods significantly enhance the predictive ability of individual methods. The realized higher-order moments of both markets can effectively increase the prediction accuracy of stock market volatility, with the higher-order moments in the stock market contributing more than those in index futures. © 2025 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Can Large Language Models forecast carbon price movements? Evidence from Chinese carbon markets
Authors: Rui Chen and Haiqi Jiang and Tingyu Guo and Chenyou Fan
Venue: Research in International Business and Finance
Abstract: This paper investigates the impact of Large Language Models (LLMs) on forecasting Chinese carbon prices. We introduce a novel two-stage forecasting framework integrating a Time-Series Model (TSM) and Large Language Models. Initially, we use historical data on Chinese Emission Allowance prices to train the TSM for preliminary predictions. LLMs then refine these predictions, which process a sequence of past and corresponding future prices as a chain of thought. Additionally, we utilize the LLM to analyze and categorize the sentiment of news headlines, generating market sentiment labels that enhance the LLM’s predictive accuracy. Our findings indicate that LLMs can improve TSM forecasts by 28–38 % across different regional markets. Furthermore, incorporating news sentiment labels into the LLM contributes an additional reduction in forecasting deviations, ranging from 3–4 %.

Title: Forecasting returns using image-based convolutional neural networks: Evidence from Korea
Authors: Jeong J.-G.; Byun S.-J.; Kim D.
Venue: Research in International Business and Finance
Abstract: This study employs a chart image-based convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict stock returns in the Korean stock market, following Jiang et al. (2023). We transform historical price and volume data into chart images and utilize CNN to extract predictive patterns. Our findings demonstrate that the CNN-based models outperform traditional benchmarks, particularly for short-term return forecasts. Additional double-sort and panel logistic regression analyses with firm characteristic variables, buy-sell imbalance analysis of investor groups, and subsample tests confirm the robustness of CNN-based predictors. This study represents the first application of a chart image-based deep learning model to the Korean stock market, providing new insights into the potential of deep learning models for stock return forecasting in emerging markets. © 2025 Elsevier B.V.
